title: NFL Trade Proposal Sees Lions Land 22.5-Sack Edge Rusher
description: The Detroit Lions could help their defense by acquiring New York Jets edge rusher Will McDonald IV. The post NFL Trade Proposal Sees Lions Land 22.5-Sack Edge Rusher appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Pundits have continuously linked the Detroit Lions to potential cornerbacks set to be available in the trade market before the NFL trade deadline. It's not hard to understand why. The Lions entered Week 5 ranked last in yards allowed, passing yards yielded and third-down defense.

But adding a cornerback isn't the only way for Detroit to improve its defense. The Lions could also aim to acquire an edge rusher.

If the Lions go that route, one potential target they could pursue currently plays for their former defensive coordinator with the New York Jets — Will McDonald IV.

Heavy Sports proposes the Lions offer a third-round pick to the Jets for McDonald.

"Will McDonald may actually be the best trade Detroit can make to improve its defense given the circumstances, even despite the fact that he could cost a late Day 2 pick," wrote Heavy Sports's Max Dible. "That is because he is young, in his fourth year, and has juice as a former first-round pick who tallied 18.5 sacks in 2024-25 combined."

Over 51 career games, McDonald has posted 22.5 sacks for the Jets. New York selected him at No. 15 overall in the 2023 NFL Draft.

The 2024 campaign remains McDonald's best season from a statistical standpoint. He registered 10.5 sacks with 11 tackles for loss and 24 quarterback hits that year. This season, he has one sack with one tackle for loss and one quarterback hit in four games.

In a perfect world, the Lions will acquire a cornerback at the trade deadline. They arguably could use multiple defensive backs to solidify their struggling secondary.

But adding a defender who could create additional pressure would help too.

"McDonald is a pass-rush specialist and isn't necessarily an every-down player," Dible wrote. But he can create quick pressures and make splash plays, which is the quickest fix for a Lions' defense that has no secondary to speak of but could line McDonald up across from Aidan Hutchinson on pass downs, thereby creating havoc and speeding up the QB clock significantly, which would help the secondary in turn.

McDonald also wouldn't be a rental player, which would help justify the team giving up a third-rounder pick for him. The edge rusher is on the fourth year of his rookie contract. The 2027 campaign will be the fifth-year option of his first NFL contract.

title: Chiefs Rookie Kahlil Benson Shares Life-Changing News After Impressive NFL Start
description: Chiefs offensive lineman Kahlil Benson has another reason to celebrate after sharing a special announcement during Kansas City's bye week. The post Chiefs Rookie Kahlil Benson Shares Life-Changing News After Impressive NFL Start appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Kansas City Chiefs rookie offensive lineman Kahlil Benson announced that he and his girlfriend, Jayda, are expecting their first child.

Benson shared the news early Saturday morning, October 10, during the Chiefs' bye week, posting a carousel of photographs on Instagram.

The announcement featured Polaroid-style pictures of the couple celebrating the pregnancy. In one photograph, a shirtless Benson held a positive pregnancy test while Jayda showed off her growing baby bump and held a sonogram.

The couple kept their announcement simple, captioning the post, "Love yours. 2027."

The caption indicates they are expecting their baby in 2027.

Benson's announcement comes during an eventful first NFL season for the former Indiana offensive lineman, who went from an undrafted rookie trying to earn a roster spot to becoming Kansas City's starting left tackle.

Benson's post drew congratulatory messages from his Kansas City teammates, including quarterback Patrick Mahomes.

"Congrats 🙏," Mahomes wrote in the comments.

Fellow rookie running back Emmett Johnson also responded to the news.

"Congrats fam 🙏," Johnson wrote.

Jayda, who uses the Instagram handle @thejaydag, identifies herself as an artist and Indiana University alumna. She also maintains a separate Instagram account dedicated to her tattoos and artwork.

The couple did not reveal their baby's sex or an exact due date in the announcement.

The personal milestone arrives shortly after Benson received one of the NFL's top monthly honors for his performance during the opening weeks of the 2026 season.

On October 1, the NFL named Benson its Offensive Rookie of the Month for September after he started Kansas City's first three games at left tackle.

Benson arrived in Kansas City in the spring as a rookie minicamp tryout player without a guaranteed contract.

The former Indiana standout impressed the coaching staff enough to earn more opportunities throughout the offseason and eventually made the Chiefs' 53-man roster.

His path to the starting lineup changed when Josh Simmons suffered a back injury that sidelined him ahead of the regular season.

Kansas City moved Benson to left tackle, a position he hadn't played in college.

The rookie made his first NFL start against the Denver Broncos on September 14, helping Kansas City secure a 31-10 victory.

Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy discussed the challenge facing Benson before his debut.

"Go play and have fun. That's all you can say," Bieniemy told reporters. "Yes, he is a young player. He's going to have some good plays, he's going to have some bad plays. But when it's all said and done with, he just needs to go out there and play and have fun."

Benson responded with a strong September performance.

According to NFL Next Gen Stats, he allowed seven quarterback pressures across 106 pass-blocking snaps during the first three games. That ranked third-fewest among NFL left tackles through the opening three weeks.

He became the first Chiefs player to win a Rookie of the Month award since linebacker Nick Bolton in October 2021.

Benson also became the first offensive lineman in the NFL to receive the monthly honor since Quenton Nelson in October 2018.

He continued starting in Kansas City's October 4 win over the Las Vegas Raiders, helping the Chiefs reach 4-0 entering their bye week.

Kansas City returns to action against the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday, October 18, at Arrowhead Stadium.

title: Mike McCarthy Reveals Steelers Are Not Alone In Early Season Struggles
description: An NFL analyst points out a shocking truth about Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy after their viral sideline clash. The coach admits the team's record tells the whole story.
fullText:
The most surprising fact after the viral sideline fight between Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy is not the anger itself, but the admission that the Steelers are not the only team feeling lost.

While fans watch the heated exchange on Thursday night, the head coach told reporters that almost every squad in the league feels just as stuck as Pittsburgh does right now. This perspective shifts the narrative from a single team's meltdown to a league-wide struggle that no one wants to admit out loud.

Mike McCarthy spent the weekend reviewing tape after the uneven loss to the Cleveland Browns, searching for answers in a game that ended with a 27-24 score. The first-year coach knows he is hardly alone in this mess. "You're hard-pressed to find a team or two that feels really good about where they are right now," he said, according to Times Observer.

This blunt assessment from the coach cuts through the noise of the viral video and suggests that the current chaos is the norm, not the exception, across the NFL.

Despite the frustration, McCarthy refuses to make excuses for the sloppy play that led to a fifth straight road setback in Cleveland. He laid out the hard truth about the team's standing with a simple shrug. "I mean, you are what you put on film and you are what your record says you are," McCarthy said. He followed that up by noting the current reality for the coaching staff and the players alike: "So, we're 2-2 as a coaching staff and as a football team."

This 2-2 record means the Steelers have won just half their games, leaving plenty of work to do before the Indianapolis Colts visit on Sunday. The team remains a work in progress, and the coach knows that looking the part is just as important as believing they can make it to January. The focus now shifts to fixing the mistakes that show up on the film before the next opponent arrives.

Instead of blaming the new system or the transition from the Mike Tomlin era, McCarthy points to his own habits as the solution. He insists that preparation is the only way to turn things around when things look wrong. "I'm a huge believer in preparation," McCarthy said.

He explained his personal approach to the problem, stating, "When it doesn't look right, I prepare more. That's the way I'm wired. That's the way I've always done it. That's what I'll continue to do, and we're going to be a better football team because of it."

This commitment to extra work is the only tool the coach has to get the team ready for a Colts squad that has been improving steadily since losing to Baltimore. The Colts have shown they can bounce back, so the Steelers must match that energy or risk falling further behind in a wide-open AFC North.

Indianapolis is not coming to Pittsburgh for a friendly visit, and their coach knows exactly how tough this game will be. Finding a way to win in the Steel City would prove that the Colts have moved past their late-season fade from last year. According to reports Shane Steichen said, "We know it's a big one."

He told his players that the challenge is huge because of the hostile environment they are walking into. The pressure is on both sides, but the Steelers must first settle their own internal issues before they can handle the pressure from the outside.

Florio's comments highlighted his concern that a quarterback's public reaction toward a head coach could affect how the rest of the team perceives its leadership. Simms acknowledged that the head coach must remain the leader, but he also emphasized the importance of veteran players holding one another accountable.

"And, you know, I think what he means too, you're right. The head coach has got to be the man, but there's got to be guys in the locker room that keep everybody held to the standard."

While Florio stressed that players should not openly undermine their head coach, Simms pointed out that experienced players can also help establish standards and hold teammates accountable.

Ultimately, the incident has sparked a broader conversation about the relationship between a veteran quarterback and his head coach. As the season continues, Pittsburgh will need to ensure that its on-field frustrations do not become a distraction from the team's performance and objectives.

One of his most famous incidents came when the was coaching the Bears in the 1992 season. The Bears had built a 20-0 lead in a road game against the Minnesota Vikings at the Metrodome. The game had reached the third quarter and Ditka wanted quarterback Jim Harbaugh to play it safe with a conservative game plan. That meant running the ball or being safe with his passes.

Shortly after sending that message to Harbaugh, the quarterback threw an out pattern that was picked off by Minnesota's Todd Scott and the defensive back brought it 35 yards for a touchdown. Ditka lit into Harbaugh with a memorable tirade that TV cameras captured.

Despite the embarrassing scene, Harbaugh and Ditka were quite close and the Chargers head coach was clearly influenced by Ditka. He reminisced about the coach following the announcement of his passing.

"I was sitting in his office and we were about to go over the gameplan," Harbaugh said. "Mike was sitting at his desk and he was writing out check after check. This went on and I asked him what he was doing. He explained that he had gotten letters from people who were struggling and needed money. I asked him if he knew the people, and he said that he didn't. He just wanted to help since they asked him."

The Miami Dolphins are searching for their first victory of the 2026 NFL season as they prepare to host the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 5. Head coach Jeff Hafley's team has lost its first four games and needs a stronger offensive performance to turn its season around.

Quarterback Malik Willis will be under pressure to improve after struggling in Miami's 15-10 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.

The Dolphins managed only 85 passing yards from Willis in that game, while a lost fumble added to their offensive problems. Miami now faces a Cincinnati defense preparing to exploit any weaknesses it has identified.

The Bengals enter the matchup with a 2-2 record, while Miami is still looking for consistency with its young roster. Ahead of Sunday's meeting at Hard Rock Stadium, comments from a Cincinnati defensive back have prompted Hafley to address one particular aspect of Willis' throwing mechanics.

Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley responds to Bengals DB Jordan Battle's statement regarding a "tell" that QB Malik Willis has #PhinsUp pic.twitter.com/DUu5g8tXU7

— c. isaiah smalls ii (@stclaudeii) October 9, 2026

Miami Herald reporter C. Isaiah Smalls II reported that Hafley responded after Cincinnati Bengals safety Jordan Battle suggested that Willis has a habit that defenders could use to anticipate his passes.

Battle previously said, "He has a little slight little tap before every throw though, so I feel like we could use that as a key to break on the ball."

"He likes to tap the ball before he throws it, or he takes his hand off, and that gives the read the break."

Battle also warned that Cincinnati must account for Willis' mobility.

He said the quarterback can extend plays and run quarterback draws on third-and-long situations, requiring defenders to remain alert even when the initial play breaks down.

Hafley, however, played down the significance of the alleged throwing tell.

The Dolphins coach said he has studied quarterbacks for more than 25 years and has seen similar movements throughout his career.

"I studied quarterbacks for over 25 years, and that is not uncommon," Hafley said Friday.

"A lot of quarterbacks pat the ball or take their hand off the ball. There are some I've studied that look up right before they throw the ball. I don't think there's anything revolutionary about that."

Hafley described the movement as a matter of timing and rhythm rather than an unusual tendency. He also welcomed Cincinnati's decision to discuss the matter publicly.

"It's a timing and rhythm thing with a lot of guys, and there's a lot of them that do that, but any opponent that wants to share our tendencies with us, we'll take any time," Hafley said.

Willis' performances give the discussion added significance.

Through four games, he has completed 56.3% of his passes for 712 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions.

He has also recorded 119 rushing yards and a rushing touchdown on 19 attempts.

After the loss to Minnesota, Willis acknowledged that the team's results and execution were not good enough.

Sunday's matchup will test whether Miami can improve against a defense that believes it has identified a potential advantage.

While Willis prepares for Cincinnati's defensive approach, Miami is also relying on its young players to help establish a stronger foundation under Hafley.

The Dolphins' rookies have combined for 1,726 snaps through four games, the most in the NFL.

Their playing time has provided valuable experience as the team continues to develop despite its 0-4 record.

Linebacker Jacob Rodriguez credited Hafley's confidence and preparation with helping him play faster and work effectively with his teammates.

"Coach Hafley gives me a lot of confidence," Rodriguez said.

"I think the confidence that he has in me instills confidence, and I have so much respect and confidence in him."

Chris Bell also expressed belief in the team's progress, emphasizing the relationships developing within the locker room.

"We work so hard week in and week out, every week," Bell said.

"And I can feel this team coming together, and we are a brotherhood, and a family."

The Dolphins now have an opportunity to translate that development into their first win.

Hafley's response to Battle has made clear that Miami does not consider Willis' throwing motion an extraordinary concern, but the quarterback must still improve his execution against Cincinnati's defense.

fullText:
Former Carolina Panthers quarterback Andy Dalton is reportedly being released by the Philadelphia Eagles, bringing an abrupt end to his time with the defending NFC East champions.

Dalton, 38, was acquired from Carolina in March in exchange for a 2027 seventh-round draft pick. But after spending three seasons as Bryce Young's backup and occasional replacement, the veteran struggled to establish himself in Philadelphia.

His regular-season numbers with the Eagles tell the story: one game, one pass attempt, zero completions and one interception.

Dalton briefly replaced Jalen Hurts during Philadelphia's Week 3 matchup against the Chicago Bears while Hurts underwent a concussion evaluation. His lone pass was intercepted in the end zone by rookie safety Dillon Thieneman.

The Eagles subsequently moved Tanner McKee ahead of Dalton on the depth chart for their Week 4 game against the Los Angeles Rams.

The #Eagles are releasing QB Andy Dalton, sources say.

Tanner McKee and Cole Payton will be the backups to Jalen Hurts moving forward. pic.twitter.com/1t9mlxFRjq

— Mike Garafolo (@MikeGarafolo) October 9, 2026

The Eagles acquired Dalton hoping his extensive NFL experience would provide insurance behind Hurts.

Dalton entered the 2026 season with 15 years of NFL experience and 169 career starts, giving Philadelphia a proven veteran option in a quarterback room that also included McKee.

However, Dalton's performance in limited regular-season action did little to strengthen his case for the backup job.

After his interception against Chicago, NFL Network reported that McKee would replace Dalton as Philadelphia's No. 2 quarterback, leaving the former Panthers starter third on the depth chart.

The decision represented a quick reversal for a quarterback Philadelphia had traded for only months earlier.

Carolina, meanwhile, had already received its return in the deal. The Panthers acquired a 2027 seventh-round draft selection while moving on from a veteran who had spent three seasons behind Young.

Dalton joined the Panthers in 2023, serving primarily as a backup while making seven starts across three seasons.

In 13 total appearances with Carolina, Dalton completed 165 of 255 passes for 1,643 yards, 10 touchdowns and seven interceptions.

His record as a Panthers starter was 1-6, although his individual performances varied considerably.

Dalton's first start for Carolina came against the Seattle Seahawks in September 2023, when he threw for 361 yards and two touchdowns in a 37-27 defeat.

His most memorable Panthers performance came the following season.

After head coach Dave Canales benched Bryce Young in September 2024, Dalton stepped in against the Las Vegas Raiders and delivered Carolina's first victory of the season.

Dalton completed 26 of 37 attempts for 319 yards and three touchdowns without an interception in the Panthers' 36-22 win.

It was an encouraging performance for Carolina, which had struggled offensively during the opening weeks of the season.

But the momentum did not last. Dalton lost his next four starts in 2024, and Young eventually reclaimed the starting job.

Dalton made one additional start during the 2025 season, completing 16 of 24 passes for 175 yards and an interception in a loss to the Buffalo Bills.

Despite his brief stint in Philadelphia, Dalton has put together an extensive NFL career dating back to 2011.

The Cincinnati Bengals selected Dalton in the second round of the 2011 NFL Draft, and he spent nine seasons as their starting quarterback.

Dalton made three Pro Bowls with Cincinnati and helped lead the Bengals to five consecutive playoff appearances from 2011 through 2015.

Across 180 regular-season appearances with the Bengals, Cowboys, Bears, Saints, Panthers and Eagles, Dalton has compiled 39,793 passing yards, 254 touchdown passes and 152 interceptions, with an 87.4 career passer rating.

His career also includes 169 starts, with most coming during his nine-year tenure in Cincinnati.

Dalton turns 39 on October 29. If his release from Philadelphia is finalized, he will become an experienced free-agent option for teams seeking quarterback depth during the 2026 season.

fullText:
In a successful and well-traveled NFL career, Andy Dalton had a stop with the New Orleans Saints.

It wasn't the most memorable or the longest, but it was substantial time on the field for "The Red Rifle" with the Saints.

It came to mind again on Friday, when the Philadelphia Eagles surprisingly released Dalton after he'd spent a portion of this season as one of the backup QBs to Jalen Hurts.

Dalton's release wasn't necessarily expected, but the Eagles did have a surplus of quarterbacks and evidently felt one of those roster spots could be used elsewhere.

The veteran Dalton wasn't in the mix to start if Hurts remained healthy, and the Eagles went with a different look for their depth chart.

Tanner McKee, the tall right-handed passer, will be Hurts' main backup. He has gotten limited starting experience in the NFL and is believed by some to be an eventual trade candidate, given that he's well thought of around the league.

The Eagles' QB3 will be Cole Payton, the athletic lefty rookie from North Dakota State. Payton is more of a project, but he's got the right traits to succeed.

Dalton played for the Saints in the 2022 NFL season.

That was after he began his career with nine years with the Cincinnati Bengals, for whom he started 133 games.

Dalton went from Cincy to the Dallas Cowboys, and he made nine starts there in 2020.

Then in 2021, Dalton went to the Chicago Bears and got six starts.

The Saints were Dalton's team in 2022, and it was his last full season of his career. He started 14 games and went 6-8. Dalton completed 66.7% of his passes for 2,871 yards with 18 touchdowns and nine interceptions.

New Orleans also had Jameis Winston start three games that season, but it was Dalton who got the lion's share of the work — along with the occasional pass by Taysom Hill.

The Saints did win a memorable 39-32 game that season over the Seattle Seahawks, in which Dalton threw one touchdown to Chris Olave. But that game was really about Hill, who completed one pass for a 22-yard touchdown to Adam Trautman and then ran nine times for 112 yards and three more TDs, including a 60-yard score.

Dalton left the Saints after that year and went to the NFC South rival Carolina Panthers, and he started seven games there over three seasons.

He joined the Eagles for the 2026 season. Dalton will turn 39 on Oct. 29, and it's not clear how much longer he may have left in the NFL.

title: Super Bowl-winning player and coach Ditka dies aged 86
description: NFL icon Mike Ditka, who coached the Chicago Bears to the Super Bowl XX title in 1986, dies aged 86.
fullText:
NFL icon and former Chicago Bears coach Mike Ditka has died aged 86.

Ditka coached the Bears to the Super Bowl XX title in 1986 and was the first tight end to be inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame.

His family confirmed the news in a statement, but no cause of death was given.

"It is with profound sadness that we announce the passing of our beloved husband, father, grandfather, and friend, Mike Ditka," said a Ditka family statement.

"While the world knew Mike as a Hall of Fame football player, legendary coach, and leader of the Chicago Bears' Super Bowl XX championship team, we knew him as the heart of our family.

"Mike will be missed beyond measure and remembered forever."

Ditka was the fifth overall pick of the 1961 draft when he joined the Bears as a player and he spent six years with the franchise before spells at the Philadelphia Eagles and the Dallas Cowboys.

He helped the Cowboys win their first Super Bowl in 1972, scoring the final touchdown in a 24-3 win against the Miami Dolphins.

Ditka enjoyed a 12-year playing career, with 427 receptions for 5,812 yards and 43 touchdowns, before retiring at the end of the 1972 season.

He was assistant coach at the Cowboys when they won the 1978 Super Bowl and went on to become Chicago Bears head coach in 1982.

Ditka created a dominant side which had a 15-1 record during the 1985-86 regular season before he led them to victory against the New England Patriots to win Super Bowl XX.

"Mike's impact on the Chicago Bears organisation, over decades as a player, coach, and proud icon and ambassador for our organisation, is immeasurable," said a Bears statement.

"His integral role in bringing world championships to our city and our franchise, both as a player and as our coach, established prominence and excellence at a world-class level, but also created a lifetime of cherished memories in the hearts and minds of Bears fans that will last for generations."

Hall of Famer Walter Payton played under Ditka and his son, Jarrett Payton, paid tribute to his father's former coach.

"Da Coach. Hall of Famer. The heartbeat of the '85 Bears and a Super Bowl champion," wrote Payton in a social media post.

fullText:
Amateur rugby union players from Hackney had a shock when they turned up for a training match - to see a former Super Bowl champion among the opposition.

Hackney RFC's players rocked up on Wednesday for a 30-minute friendly, only to find former NFL star Jason Kelce playing for local rivals Old Streetonians.

Kelce - older brother of Travis, the three-time Super Bowl winning Kansas City Chiefs tight end married to global pop superstar Taylor Swift - played 13 seasons with the Philadelphia Eagles.

The 38-year-old is now learning to play different sports for his YouTube channel, and had a rugby lesson from former Harlequins and England prop Joe Marler.

"It's a nice little story being able to say we played rugby against Taylor Swift's brother-in-law, which I'm sure he loves as a title," Hackney full-back Peter Scott joked to BBC Sport.

"It's amazing that the sporting community, not even just the rugby community, can make these sorts of things happen. It was pretty surreal and it's pretty cool."

Kelce was part of Philadelphia's 2018 Super Bowl winning side and earned seven selections to the Pro Bowl - the annual NFL game featuring the league's top players - before retiring in 2024.

He was joined by former Philadelphia team-mate Beau Allen, also a member of that Eagles championship side of eight years ago, at Hackney Marshes in London this week.

Hackney prop Dave Lewis told BBC Sport it took Kelce - a former center, an offensive lineman, whose main role is to snap the ball to the quarterback and then protect him, each play - a while to get used to rugby's rules.

"We got a message from our club captain saying our local rivals were coming down with two ex-NFL players, but we didn't know anything else about it," Lewis said.

"With the rules, he got there. At the very start, he sort of went round the back of a ruck and picked the ball up, which he obviously was then penalised for.

"I handed him off at one point and put him on his back in front of his team-mates and all of our fans as well. I hope they release that footage because I'll be dining out on it forever if they do.

"He just got back up and absolutely smashed me later on when he had the ball, running through me. So, I don't think he has an ego. I think he's just up for the physicality of it all."

Lewis' team-mate Scott said he thought Kelce picked the game up pretty quickly.

"He's a pretty intimidating figure," Scott added. "Very broad shoulders, powerful legs. They were using him as a number 8, which, I think, is the perfect position for him.

"There were a few intricacies, like how he was carrying the ball and where he was in the scrum, but he clearly knew what he was. He didn't look out of place at all.

"In rugby you are taught to tackle at an angle, and go at people's shoulders. He was a lot more front on, like 'OK, route one, I'm just gonna go straight at anyone that came out'."

Kelce is in England this week to commentate on Sunday's NFL overseas game between his former club Philadelphia and the Jacksonville Jaguars at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium (14:30 BST).

Old Street chairman Will Gilgrass said both Kelce and Allen really embraced the whole opportunity.

"They were very good value in the pub afterwards," he said. "We took them to one of our locals, and they put their cards behind the bar, chatting with the lads for a few hours after the game and really getting involved.

"They even did our initiation, singing a song and downing a pint."

The Hackney players also had their 15 minutes of fame after the match, with Kelce's American film crew interviewing some of them.

"They were asking how he got on, and what were the major differences to translate to an NFL audience," said Scott.

"The one I picked up on was the amount of power that he was able to generate after he would get tackled. His leg drives were sensational. It felt like three people would hit him and then he would go for another 20 metres.

"American football seems to be all about short, sharp, explosive power and he had that in spades - like he was rapid, very powerful, and then would take a backseat for a little while and then come back and do it again."

title: NFL predictions: Can Falcons overcome Ravens on Sunday Night Football?
description: The Falcons offense looks balanced and unstoppable, and now enters a third-straight primetime matchup: Sunday Night Football against the Baltimore Ravens in Week 5.
fullText:
The Falcons emerge from Week 4's Monday Night Football matchup with the hated Saints as glorious victors, dominating on a level I previously assumed was impossible. Atlanta's 45-24 humiliation of New Orleans on such a historic night is nothing short of astonishing, and requires a re-evaluation of what we all believed this Falcons team could be just a few weeks ago.

After an 0-2 start where the team managed just 8 points per game (32nd) under third-string quarterback Cooper Rush, the Falcons have now averaged 40 points per game (1st) under starter Michael Penix Jr. Bijan Robinson is as dominant as ever, and his complement in Brian Robinson has also impressed. The Falcons offense looks balanced and unstoppable, and now enters a third-straight primetime matchup: Sunday Night Football against the Baltimore Ravens in Week 5. The Falcons are 3.5-point home favorites per FanDuel—the first time Atlanta has been favored this season—implying a tight game, particularly if injuries impact the Ravens starting lineup.

The biggest thing to monitor heading into this game is the injury report. Baltimore seems likely to be without MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson, as he missed practice on both Wednesday and Thursday. It's not impossible for Lamar to suit up, but Atlanta will probably face veteran backup Tyler Huntley on Sunday night. This Ravens offense has been quite potent over the first four weeks of the 2026 season: 7th in scoring and 5th in total yards. But it's unlikely that type of production will continue with Huntley in the lineup, as Jackson's dynamic athleticism and playmaking ability raise the ceiling tremendously.

Baltimore's offensive line is also very banged up. The Ravens are down multiple centers are were forced to move rookie guard Vega Ioane into the middle. A trade for Cam Jurgens will provide long-term help, but Jurgens is not expected to play on Sunday. Left guard John Simpson has been limited with a groin injury, and reserve guard Andrew Vorhees (who is starting at right guard with Ioane at center) is dealing with a foot injury. Left tackle Ronnie Stanley is battling through toe and ankle injuries, but is expected to play.

This is very bad news for the Ravens, with the Falcons boasting the league's top run defense and the league's top pass rush in pressures. Atlanta's ability to dominate the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball is part of what led to their lopsided victories over the past two weeks. Baltimore is a far better opponent than either Green Bay or New Orleans, even with Tyler Huntley, but that's a tough matchup to deal with.

On the other side of the ball, top edge rusher Trey Hendrickson and corner Marlon Humphrey both missed practice to start the week. This is the best defense the Falcons have faced yet, even with those two potentially out of the lineup, both those are major losses against a red-hot offense. Atlanta is the second-best rushing attack in the NFL (including the two Cooper Rush starts) and has allowed the lowest pressure rate in the league on offense.

Those mounting injuries—along with the road trip to an Atlanta stadium that will likely be the most raucous it's been in years after two straight blowout victories—could lead to a very difficult environment for the Ravens to have success. However, this is a well-coached team that's still got talent all over the roster, and they're not just going to roll over for the Falcons.

All that being said, if Tyler Huntley plays, I'm not sure the Ravens will be able to get enough out of the passing game to keep pace with the Falcons offensively. Atlanta's defense can be vulnerable to big plays in the passing game, but I don't think Huntley is the type of quarterback who can take advantage. The Falcons will be loading up to stop Derrick Henry and crowding the short area of the field to take away quick play-action and YAC throws. This will be by far the best rushing attack Atlanta has had to defend, and we're going to learn if the team's elite run defense is capable of shutting down one of the best running backs in the NFL.

The Ravens defense will put up more of a fight than either of their past two opponents, and I'd expect Atlanta's offense to sputter a bit out of the gate. But the Falcons are simply too good on the ground to hold down for long, and the more Baltimore sells out to stop the run, the more downfield opportunities will present themselves for Michael Penix Jr. This could be a bigger test for Penix, as the Ravens will likely opt to "make Penix beat us". Working out of play-action and finding the right times to attack downfield will be critical to keep the defense honest.

An injury-marred Ravens team helmed by Tyler Huntley would've been a classic trap game for the Falcons under Raheem Morris. That's a game this team would almost always find a way to lose, despite the matchups largely falling in their favor. I know Baltimore will put up a fight regardless of who is behind center, and Atlanta should be prepared for a brawl—particularly in the first half. Atlanta starts to wear down the Ravens in the second half, and ultimately comes away with the Sunday Night Football victory, 27-20.

title: Panthers' Bryce Young leaps up NFL QB rankings

After a rough Week 3, Bryce Young returned to form in Week 4, dicing up Detroit's defense by focusing heavily on throws in the middle third of the field and feasting, even without Jalen Coker. The only non-excellent start Young has had this season was the loss to Cleveland in Week 3. While he didn't perform well, it wouldn't be fair to put much blame on him given his poor protection and absence of his No. 2 and No. 3 wideouts.

In Young's other three starts, he's been nothing less than brilliant—making the right choices in quick fashion. His processing has largely neutralized what has been the worst pressure rate for any quarterback in the league this year.

title: Jason Kelce shares insight on former Philadelphia Eagles teammate Lane Johnson’s retirement
description: Future Hall of Famer Lane Johnson announced his retirement from the NFL earlier this week. The Philadelphia Eagles will now be without their star offensive lineman for the first time since drafting him in 2013.
fullText:
Future Hall of Famer Lane Johnson announced his retirement from the NFL earlier this week. The Philadelphia Eagles will now be without their star offensive lineman for the first time since drafting him in 2013.

Johnson earned six Pro Bowl selections and five All-Pro honours during his career, and he won two Super Bowls with the Eagles (LII and LIX). Philadelphia won 66 percent of the games he played in, compared to just 38 percent of the games he missed.

The 36-year-old will be remembered as one of the greatest offensive linemen of his generation, and few know him better than Jason Kelce. His former Eagles teammate has now shared some insight into what Johnson may be going through following his retirement.

Jason Kelce, a former member of the Philadelphia Eagles' NFL-leading offensive line with Lane Johnson, knows how difficult retirement can be. While he appreciated the opportunity to leave on his own terms, it did not make his decision easy.

Kelce revealed that he spoke to Johnson before his own retirement in 2024, and more recently, about Johnson's retirement. He explained the challenge Johnson would have faced to play another season without being 100 percent focused, suggesting he made the right decision.

"This was his 14th season," Kelce said. "Whenever you get older, it's something you think about. I certainly thought about it for the last four years before I ended up making the decision.

"It becomes really hard to play football when you're on the north side of 35 years old, especially up front at the offensive line position. You're playing through things and your life is changing. There's a lot going on.

"I remember talking to Lane for many years about when it was right for me to stop playing. We've certainly had those discussions with Lane before…

"He's one of the few players who was so good that everyone is still chomping at the bit to get him to play. The reality is that if you're not 100 percent in, this is a sport that's very hard to do, and I trust that he felt it was the time to stop."

title: Why Chiefs Star Kenneth Walker Deserves MVP Through First Quarter Of NFL Season
description: Kenneth Walker is the main reason the Chiefs, the only undefeated team in the AFC, has become an explosive offense once again.
fullText:
Last year's Super Bowl MVP could very well become the ensuing season's regular-season MVP.

Through the quarter mark of the season — or what would've been so before the NFL went from 16 games to 17 in 2021 — Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker has been the most valuable player in all of football.

Last year's Chiefs team finished 6-11 and had the 25th-ranked rushing offense.

Now they're the only undefeated team in the AFC and have third best running game in the NFL.

Sure, two-time, regular-season MVP Patrick Mahomes has made a remarkable recovery from reconstructive knee surgery, but last year the Chiefs lacked big-chunk plays in the running game.

During the whole season, running back Kareem Hunt had one 33-yard run, and Isiah Pacheco's longest run was just 16 yards.

In 2026 Walker, the NFL's leading rusher, is one explosive play waiting to happen. He already tops all running backs with six plays of runs of more than 20 yards.

Walker began the season by turning a 4th-and-1 play into a 60-yard touchdown run.

His latest game-changing play came at the end of the third quarter in a game that the Las Vegas Raiders had led for the majority, and it went for 76 yards.

"Man, that's normal for him," Chiefs wide receiver Xavier Worthy said. "We just tell him to take over."

Walker took over the Week Four game when the Chiefs lined up in three-tight-end set. He then ran between the blocks of right guard Trey Smith and right tackle Jaylon Moore. According to Zebra Technologies' analytics, the play was only expected to gain five yards.

Gaining extra yards had been Walker's modus operandi. Not only does he have the speed to outrun defenders, but he also has a knack for breaking their tackles.

He leads the NFL in missed tackles forced this season with 43, and the next highest is Detroit Lions superstar Jahmyr Gibbs, who is 15 behind.

The MVP has basically been a quarterback award of late.

The last running back — and also non-quarterback — to win it was Minnesota Vikings running back Adrian Peterson in 2012.

Peterson rushed for 2,097 in 16 games, and Walker is on pace for 2,282 in 17 games. That would break the single-season mark Eric Dickerson set in the 16-game, 1984 season.

So Walker earning MVP honors would be historic — and valuable in more ways than one.

The last two winners were Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford in 2025 and Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen in 2024. Stafford was in the middle of a two-year, $84 million extension, and Allen was on a six-year, $258 million extension.

Walker would represent a much cheaper alternative as MVP. He is in the first year of a three-year, $43.05 million contract.

And the player with 537 rushing yards does more than run the ball. He has opened up the passing game.

Because of the threat of Walker and the run game, the Chiefs are using the play-action passing game more than ever.

On the very first play of Week Three, a play-action fake to Walker led to Travis Kelce being wide open down the field and to a 48-yard gain — the game's longest play.

A three-down back, Walker already has 84 receiving yards, which is on pace for a career high of 357.

"I could always catch the ball," Walker said. "I just didn't really have opportunities to catch the ball. Coach (Andy) Reid sees that I can catch and make plays in space. So I feel like that's like credit to Coach Reid."

And credit to Chiefs general manager Brett Veach for acquiring Walker in what is shaping up to be the wisest NFL signing this year.

title: NFL suspends two officials for player incidents

title: ‘Did Not Think This Would Actually Happen,’ ‘Backfield Gets Even Messier’ — NFL World Has Mixed Reactions to Joe Mixon Signing With Seahawks After Mystery Injury
description: The Seattle Seahawks are in the process of adding running back Joe Mixon to their practice squad after working him out Monday, coach Mike Macdonald said, and early takes from people on social media weighed his health against Seattle’s crowded backfield. NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported on Monday that Seattle is signing Mixon, who will wear jersey No.
fullText:
The Seattle Seahawks are in the process of adding running back Joe Mixon to their practice squad after working him out Monday, coach Mike Macdonald said, and early takes from people on social media weighed his health against Seattle's crowded backfield.

NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported on Monday that Seattle is signing Mixon, who will wear jersey No. 25. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that the plan is to sign the veteran running back to the practice squad once he completes his medical exam.

Mixon, a two-time Pro Bowler, missed all of 2025 with a foot injury, and the Houston Texans released him in March. Texans general manager Nick Caserio called the injury "kind of a freak thing" in January.

In July, KPRC-2 Houston's Aaron Wilson reported that Mixon had told former Bengals teammates he was done playing and that he had dealt with blood flow problems in his foot and had recently undergone another surgery on it. He added that a source close to Mixon still saw some hope of a return.

SleeperSeahawks, a Seahawks news account, was struck by how quickly things changed over the last 48 hours. "He must be healthy!" SleeperSeahawks wrote.

Fox Sports' Jay Glazer had reported a day earlier that Seattle was bringing Mixon in for a visit. Schultz reported later Monday that Seattle wanted to make sure Mixon was in shape and came away impressed with his conditioning, and that Mixon will start on the practice squad.

For The Latest Information: NFL Injury Report

A fan drew the same conclusion about the foot. "They wouldn't sign Mixon if the foot was bad," the fan wrote, adding that a healthy Mixon could earn a real role fast.

Mixon was productive the last time he played. He ran for 1,016 yards, 15th in the NFL, and 11 touchdowns on 245 carries for Houston in 2024, and he has 7,428 career rushing yards in 111 games. His last game was a Divisional Round playoff game at Kansas City on Jan. 18, 2025.

Seattle ON Tap, a Seattle sports fan account, expressed surprise and hope for a healthy Mixon in his prime. "Did not think this would actually happen," Seattle ON Tap wrote.

Seattle also has a need at the position. The defending Super Bowl champions, 3-1 after Sunday's 30-23 win over the Los Angeles Chargers, put first-round rookie Jadarian Price on injured reserve Saturday with a chest injury, and Kenneth Walker III, the Super Bowl MVP, signed with the Kansas City Chiefs in March.

SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN's Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer

One fan, replying to Schefter's report, wrote that a practice-squad start for a two-time Pro Bowler shows Seattle "wants to see the legs before handing him anything." The fan called it a low-risk move with Price on injured reserve.

Mixon would join the backfield Emanuel Wilson carried against the Chargers. Wilson, who is ranked 42nd on PFN's RB Impact Metric, ran 21 times for 81 yards and a touchdown and caught three passes for 39 yards and another score, while George Holani had 18 yards on seven carries.

Sports analyst Max Loeb, eager to see how the group looks with Charbonnet due back soon, still sided with the incumbent. "Adding him in Fantasy if my team is in a good spot/I have the room, still feel like it's Wilson's backfield," Loeb wrote.

Wilson has 190 yards on 53 carries through Week 4, an average of 3.6 per carry. According to Next Gen Stats, his rush yards over expected stand at -19 through Week 4, tying him for 36th among 45 qualified rushers.

FantasyPros analyst Derek Brown was blunter. "A mess of a backfield gets even messier," Brown wrote.

Charbonnet is working back, too. He tore his ACL in January's Divisional Round win over the San Francisco 49ers, had surgery on Feb. 20, and returned to practice Thursday.

"He's going to get team reps this week, which is really exciting," Macdonald told Seattle Sports' Brock and Salk on Monday. He also said Charbonnet will not play against the 49ers in Week 5.

Seattle has until Oct. 22 to add Charbonnet to the 53-man roster, or he must remain on the physically unable to perform list for the rest of the season.

Yahoo Fantasy Sports, Yahoo's fantasy account, poked fun at the logjam.

"Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet fantasy managers watching the Seahawks sign Joe Mixon," Yahoo Fantasy Sports wrote.

Mixon is not headed straight to the active roster. Macdonald said he would join the practice squad, and Schefter reported that Mixon was still completing his medical exam on Monday.

Fantasy football podcast host and writer Brian Drake went further. "Whenever an agent uses the word "talented" in their insider leaks, you know it's over. Mixon is toast. Don't bother adding him in fantasy," Drake wrote, telling fantasy managers not to bother adding him and pointing them to Wilson, Holani and Charbonnet instead.

The Seahawks host the 4-0 49ers on Sunday without Price or Charbonnet, then face the Denver Broncos four days later.

title: Aidan Hutchinson Sends Blunt Message to Fans Amid Lions Struggles

fullText:
The Detroit Lions defense is the worst in the NFL through four weeks. While star edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson is having a good season, he is the leader of this unit and is taking accountability for the struggles.

Hutchinson was asked what can be said by him and his teammates, not only in the locker room, but to the frustrated fans. The Lions' four-year, $180M star edge rusher made it clear that nothing can be said right now because talk is cheap."

"I'm so tired of talk," declared Hutchinson on the discussions going on in the locker room. "To me, talk is cheap. If you really want to do something, let's go win the damn game and make the plays we need to make."

Hutchinson was fired up when discussing what the team needs to do.

However, when he was asked what the team can do on paper, or within the scheme, to change things, he admitted that he is just as stumped as defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard.

"I'm not sure right now," admitted Hutchinson. "I'm kind of still analyzing and trying to figure out what is going wrong."

However, Hutchinson made it clear to fans that he is not quitting on the team despite the slow start. He still sees things turning around and the team making the most of this.

"I'm going to stay in it," said Hutchinson. "I am going to keep improving individually and try to do anything I can do to help our team win."

The Lions star told fans not to quit and to stay in it with him. He noted that he sees a semblance of a dangerous team. They just need to put everything together.

"I know we're going to figure it out," said Hutchinson. "And when we do, when we're clicking on all cylinders, we're going to be such a dangerous team."

Detroit is still 2-2 despite the defense. If they can get the defense figured out, the offense is going to help them win games.

The Lions' secondary gets a lot of the bad reputation on the defense, and that is rightfully so. However, the edge rusher group outside of Hutchinson is also a disappointment.

Hutchinson has 29 pressures on 182 pass rush snaps. He has a 27.1% win rate and a 9.9 pass-rush productivity rate per PFF. D.J. Wonnum is second on the team with eight pressures on 128 pass-rush snaps.

He has a 4.7 PRP and an 11% win rate. Tyler Lacy has 51 pass rush snaps and a 3.1 PRP, with a 6.3% win rate. Lastly is rookie Derrick Moore. The second-round pick has just 29 pass rush snaps. Moore has three pressures and a 5.4 PRP. He has a disappointing 3.6% pass-rush win rate.

The secondary is a problem, but the three rushers behind Hutchinson have not carried their weight. Hutchinson can only do so much. The others need to step up.

title: ‘I’ll Always Take the Blame,’ ‘I Don’t Have No Comment’ — Todd Bowles’ Job Security in Question as Buccaneers Drop to 0-4
description: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers fell to 0-4 on Sunday with a 17-14 home loss to the Green Bay Packers in undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels’ first NFL start, and coach Todd Bowles said the blame belonged to his team. “It’s on us,” Bowles said.
fullText:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers fell to 0-4 on Sunday with a 17-14 home loss to the Green Bay Packers in undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels' first NFL start, and coach Todd Bowles said the blame belonged to his team.

"It's on us," Bowles said. "We know what the problem is. It's on us. We can't keep getting close and not winning. That's not good enough."

Tampa Bay lost its first three games 33-27 at Cincinnati, 23-19 to Cleveland and 23-16 to Minnesota, making Sunday its fourth straight loss by seven points or fewer. The Buccaneers are 0-4 for the first time since 2013, according to the team.

Some fans called for Bowles to go, and two-time All-Pro tackle Tristan Wirfs declined to comment when asked about his coach's job security.

"I don't have no comment," Wirfs said when asked what he would tell ownership in Bowles' defense. "I love coach Bowles, yeah, I don't know."

Wirfs put the burden on the players. "No one is coming to save us," he said. "We aren't going to magically get a superhero in here." He added, "It's the guys in this locker room that are going to get us out of it."

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

Pewter Report, which covers the Buccaneers, posted video of Wirfs' answer and described it as his reaction to "a question about Todd Bowles' job security."

Bowles took the blame himself. "I'm the head coach," he said. "I can do more. I can always do more. I'll always take the blame." He also said the team would stay together. "We're gonna fight, we're gonna stick together and we're gonna figure this thing out," Bowles added. "And I'll lead them to that. It's my job."

The Buccaneers marked the end of the game with a one-word post, "Final." "Embarrassing clean house," one fan replied. "It's time for Bowles to retire," another wrote.

Daniels completed 19 of 27 passes for 148 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions, and he ran eight times for 55 yards. Green Bay turned the interceptions into 10 points, including Trey Smack's 58-yard field goal as the first half ended.

Jordan Love threw 2-yard touchdown passes to Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft, and the Packers led 17-7 until Daniels hit Kenny Gainwell for a 10-yard score early in the fourth quarter. Tampa Bay's defense then forced two turnovers, a fumble recovered by Zyon McCollum at the Buccaneers' 4 and a Jacob Parrish interception at the 7, but neither led to points.

The last drive reached the Green Bay 46 before safety Evan Williams came in unblocked on fourth-and-11 and Daniels' throw fell incomplete with 1:25 left. Daniels took responsibility for the protection. "If I flip that and make sure that we're able to slide to him, he doesn't get free and I'm able to make a throw," he said.

Before that play, Bowles passed on what would have been a 65-yard field-goal attempt by Chase McLaughlin, whose career long of 65 yards came last season. "It was too far for us, a good 10 to 15 yards too far for us," Bowles said. "The wind was blowing that way as well. We thought about it, didn't feel good about it."

One fan asked "why not give Chase a chance to kick it" and took aim at Bowles and offensive coordinator Zac Robinson. "I can't wait to pay for Bowles and Zac Robinson Uber to Tampa International Airport," the fan wrote, adding that the "Defense & Special Teams played good enough and Offense line failed the test again."

Daniels was sacked three times, and Tampa Bay has allowed 16 sacks in four games. Love completed 22 of 30 passes for 197 yards and was not sacked.

Another fan took a sarcastic shot at the timeout Tampa Bay called just before Smack's kick. "The Bucs are 0-4, we love Todd Bowles for icing the kicker at the half, those 3 points lost them the game," the fan wrote.

The loss was Tampa Bay's 11th in its last 13 games dating to last season, when the Bucs opened 6-2 before losing seven of their final nine to miss the playoffs. The Buccaneers had won four division titles and a Super Bowl in the previous six seasons. Bowles is under contract through 2028, according to The Associated Press.

Pewter Report noted that Bowles "will not speak on the team's extended struggles going back to last year, but he did speak on starting the year 0-4."

Only one team in NFL history, the 1992 San Diego Chargers, has made the playoffs after an 0-4 start, according to the team. Bowles kept his focus on the next game. "We're just trying to get a win against the Cowboys, then we'll go from there," he said.

BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN's Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator

One fan responded to FOX Sports NFL writer Greg Auman's video of Bowles' postgame remarks. "He can say that all day, and he does," the fan wrote. "But nothing is happening to change it. It's all talk." He added, "It's been time for a change since January of 2025."

Daniels will start again Thursday. "Yeah, he'll be the quarterback Thursday night," Bowles said. "He had some ups and he had some downs, but for his first time out there, he didn't panic, he didn't do anything. He escaped, used his legs well at times."

Baker Mayfield, who had started 57 consecutive games for Tampa Bay including the postseason, dislocated his right thumb late in the Week 3 loss to Minnesota and is expected to miss at least two more games.

The Buccaneers visit the Dallas Cowboys (2-2) on Thursday night. Dallas beat Houston 34-30 on Sunday.

title: 'Money-grab' or celebration? NFL kicks off London series
description: The NFL kicked off this season's series of London games on Sunday but the build-up was overshadowed by anger from long-term fans over ticket prices.
fullText:
Once upon a time, tickets for NFL games in London were like gold dust.

All 43 games have been near capacity at Wembley, Twickenham and Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

According to the NFL, its UK fanbase has swelled to 18.6 million, with 4.5 million of those considered 'avid' fans.

So in the build-up to this year's London series, why were thousands of tickets still available for two of the three games?

Next week's clash between the Philadelphia Eagles and Jacksonville Jaguars at Tottenham sold out in hours.

But the crowd for Sunday's game at Tottenham between Washington Commanders and Indianapolis Colts only reached 60,907 after ticket prices were slashed, and large sections remain unsold for the Wembley game on 18 October.

The NFL is playing a record nine regular-season games abroad this season but 19 years after the first London game, has the NFL reached a saturation point in the UK?

Tickets to see Indianapolis beat Washington 30-13 on Sunday went on sale in July at £79-£245.

But the NFL then dropped prices twice, in late August and again last week. That meant some fans who paid £185 were sat next to fans who paid £79 a few days ago.

Some tickets were also discounted or free via the Blue Light Card and Tickets For Good platforms.

Matt Cullen has travelled from Cambridge to most of the London games and said there were two main reasons for the slow sales; a price hike and a season-ticket package being scrapped.

"I find the prices now mind-boggling," he added. "It's so far above the rate of inflation that it just feels like a money-grab. It's priced out a lot of long-term fans."

In 2019, tickets ranged from £55 to £125. According to Ticket-Compare,, external UK inflation has since risen by about 32.4% and the cheapest NFL London tickets have risen by 43.9%. The most expensive have seen a 96.5% hike.

Season-ticket packages had been available, guaranteeing seats for each London game with a discount, but they were scrapped after the 2024 season.

"It felt like a kick to the head for a lot of loyal fans who'd supported the games for a long time and spent a lot of money," said Cullen, a former season-ticket holder. "But I do understand the NFL wants to bring new fans in."

UK fans have also complained about the quality of recent match-ups in London when compared to those in the new countries where the NFL has expanded.

Australia hosted a divisional clash between the San Francisco 49ers and Los Angeles Rams last month, while the Baltimore Ravens and Dallas Cowboys played out a thriller in Brazil last week.

"It was an amazing game and we haven't had many of those unfortunately," added Cullen.

The best team coming to London this year is Philadelphia, who have reached two of the past four Super Bowls, and their game next week is a sell-out even though it was the most expensive.

The Jaguars face the Houston Texans in two weeks and Dave, another former season-ticket holder, will travel from Chorley.

"We were all gutted when they took the season tickets away," he admitted. "The way we saw it, we weren't wanted anymore because we didn't spend the money that new fans do on merchandise and we get to the stadium later.

"But it has opened it up for more fans to have the opportunity to attend so it's a double-edged sword."

BBC Sport spoke to dozens of fans at Sunday's game and none of them were aware ticket prices had dropped. None seemed to care either.

American fans know the London games don't provide the same tailgating experience they get back home, but they - and the players - are still fascinated by the eclectic crowd at international games.

Fans still travel from all over the UK, Europe and the US, wearing jerseys of all the NFL teams.

"It's still one of the greatest sporting events that neutrals can go to," said Dave. "I don't think there's any other sport where you'd get tens of thousands watching teams they don't support.

"It was always a celebration of the game. People would go for the love of the sport rather than the two teams that were playing and I think that's still the same."

It sure felt like a Washington home game when they recovered a Colts fumble on just the game's second play.

The crowd produced an even bigger roar when third-choice quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis - replacing the injured Marcus Mariota - made a 47-yard touchdown pass to Treylon Burks in the third quarter.

The Commanders thought they had drawn level when Antonio Williams ran in an 87-yard score, but the touchdown was chalked off for a Washington penalty.

Indianapolis quarterback Daniel Jones then got in to seal their success, with Jonathan Taylor having run in two touchdowns for the Colts.

It is hard to imagine anyone went home disappointed, no matter what price they paid.

The stands were bathed in sunshine and fans looked like they were having the time of their life as they sang Sweet Caroline and Wonderwall in unison.

Oasis' Noel Gallagher was booed when he appeared on the big screen - no doubt because of his football allegiance to Manchester City - and former Manchester United and England striker Wayne Rooney was also among the crowd, wearing a half-and-half scarf.

Olympian Simone Biles travelled to London to support her husband Jonathan Owens, who is a safety for the Colts, and as long as stars such as those show up at NFL games, international fans will want to be there too.

"There's been a lot of anger from fans on social media about the ticket prices but it's only what they do with last-minute holidays," added Dave.

"Even though some of us fans see it as poor way for the NFL to run it, they've got a full stadium.

"We're just not used to dynamic pricing in the UK. It was the same with Oasis tickets for their reunion. We were outraged at that but we still all went didn't we."

title: Efton Chism III’s amazing one-handed TD catch might have saved the Patriots’ season
description: The NFL’s best catch this season came from a totally anonymous wide receiver.
fullText:
Drake Maye has been absolutely dreadful to start the 2026 season to follow a breakout second season that almost earned him league MVP. Maye and the New England Patriots badly needed a win over Buffalo Bills in Week 4 to build some positive momentum and avoid a 1-3 start. Maye played by far his best game of the season, and he gave the Patriots a chance to win by hooking up with wide receiver Efton Chism III for a clutch fourth quarter touchdown.

With the Bills leading by five points late in the fourth quarter, Maye rolled to his right and flung the ball to the end zone. Chism seemed to be held by Buffalo's defensive back when the ball was in the air, but that didn't stop him from extended his free arm to make an incredible one-handed catch to take the lead. New England picked off Josh Allen on the next possession, and the Patriots earned the win they were desperate to get.

Did Chism make the best catch of the year so far? I think so given the stakes. Apologies to Keon Coleman, who also made an amazing catch in this game, but this is at least the catch of the week. Watch Chism's grab here:

ARE YOU EFTON KIDDING ME!!!!!!!

📺 CBS pic.twitter.com/dRQyU4Vbca

Chism was an undrafted free agent in 2025 who only had five career catches coming into this week. Chism entered the game with two catches for -1 yard on the season. A receiver with this small of a footprint making arguably the best catch of the season, and one that delivered New England a victory at that, is a truly special moment.

Maye will get the credit for leading the Patriots to a bounce-back win against an elite team, but it doesn't happen without Chism making this ridiculous and amazing play for his QB. The NFL never ceases to surprise us.

"He looks like a rookie, and not a particularly good one," one AFC scout told Vacchiano. "If he were anyone else, based on those three games, the [coaching] staff would say, 'He's just not ready yet.' But how do you say that about a guy who nearly won MVP?"

"His confidence is completely gone, and you can see why," the scout added, per Vacchiano. "He's making comical errors — like real rookie stuff. The ball popping out of his hand, lofting it towards tightly covered receivers with no zip on the ball, not seeing any of the coverage in the area and thinking a guy is open, not stepping up in the pocket to avoid the rush, or stepping up into it. It seems like every other decision he makes is wrong."

Mayfield is expected to miss three to six weeks, according to NFL insider Adam Schefter. The exact timeline will depend on when the veteran quarterback can grip the football well enough to return.

fullText:
NFL players received 22 unsportsmanlike conduct fines totaling $300,089 in Week 2, creating one of the most expensive stretches of the young season.

The league's latest accountability report showed a very different picture in Week 3. Five players received unsportsmanlike conduct fines totaling $63,908, representing a 78.7% decline from the previous week.

The NFL fined Lee Hunter, Quinn Meinerz, Jaylen Waddle, Mack Hollins and Abdul Carter for unsportsmanlike conduct in Week 3.

Meinerz and Waddle were fined $14,926 each for illegal celebrations and vulgar acts. Hunter received a $10,174 fine for taunting, while Hollins and Carter were each fined $11,941 for taunting.

Those five fines totaled $63,908. That was $236,181 less than the $300,089 that players were fined for unsportsmanlike conduct in Week 2.

The number of fines also fell sharply. Week 2 produced 22 unsportsmanlike conduct fines, compared to only five in Week 3. That represents a 77.3% decrease.

Hollins also received a separate $22,500 fine for unnecessary roughness involving the use of his helmet on the same play as his taunting violation. That fine is not included in the Week 3 unsportsmanlike conduct total.

The league recorded 30 fined plays across all violation categories in Week 3, down from 38 in Week 2.

In Week 2, the NFL handed out 22 fines for unsportsmanlike conduct to just 13 players. The penalties covered everything from illegal celebrations and taunting to vulgar acts and obscene gestures, with several players getting hit with multiple fines.

Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase received two $14,926 fines for obscene gestures. Teammate Tee Higgins received four fines, including three for obscene gestures and one for an illegal celebration or vulgar act.

Detroit Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown received four fines for illegal celebrations and vulgar acts. Jahmyr Gibbs and Penei Sewell were also fined for the same violation, while Jameson Williams received separate fines for taunting and an illegal celebration.

San Francisco 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk received two $14,926 fines for duplicating his 'Juice' chugging celebration against the Miami Dolphins, which the NFL ruled an offensive demonstration. Teammate Upton Stout was fined $7,501 for taunting during the same game.

Week 3 still produced several notable fines, but the volume did not approach what players faced one week earlier. Unsportsmanlike conduct accounted for only five of the league's 30 fined plays, bringing the combined cost down by nearly 79%.

JJ McCarthy's Minnesota Vikings tenure may have unraveled. However, his arrival with the New York Giants could give the former first-round pick a much-needed second chance. At least one NFL quarterback evaluator believes McCarthy can rebuild his career in New York. A familiar coaching connection and reduced expectations could help him regain his footing.

Speaking to FOX Sports, the evaluator pointed to head coach John Harbaugh's connection to his brother, Jim Harbaugh, who coached McCarthy at Michigan, as a potential advantage.

"A fresh start with people that chose him is a good thing," the evaluator said. "The Harbaugh history helps, too. Matt Nagy, I would think, knows what he's doing, too."

McCarthy also will not immediately carry the burden of rescuing the Giants' franchise. With Jaxson Dart sidelined by knee surgery, veteran Jameis Winston will handle the starting job. The evaluator compared the situation to quarterbacks such as Mac Jones, Sam Darnold, and Baker Mayfield. They found opportunities to reset their careers after difficult initial stops.

Ladd McConkey has battled injuries throughout the 2026 season, and while he is officially questionable with a foot injury, he should suit up for Week 4's battle against the Seattle Seahawks. Originally entering the league as a second-round pick in the 2024 NFL Draft, the Georgia product took the league by storm and immeidately established himself as one of Justin Herbert's most reliable targets. Starting in 14 games while making 16 appearances, the wideout finished his inaugural campaign with 82 receptions for 1,149 yards and seven touchdowns on 112 targets. While he wasn't quite as effective in Year 2, he remained a key part of the offense.

Now entering Week 4, Ladd McConkey has been one of the few consistent weapons in the Los Angeles Chargers offense, and he should suit up for a must-win game against the Seattle Seahawks. While nothing is official as of this posting, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport tweeted that the pass-catcher is "likely to play today."

It's hard to overstate just how important Ladd McConkey is for the Chargers to have any shot at pulling an upset against the Seattle Seahawks. While the Los Angeles offense has struggled to reach its ceiling under offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, McConkey has found a way to record 12 receptions for 183 yards and a touchdown despite playing through a variety of injuries.

It's hard to call any game a "must-win" this early in the season, but that's exactly what Week 4 is for the Los Angeles Chargers. At 0-3, the team is already three games behind the Kansas City Chiefs and Las Vegas Raiders for the AFC West crown, and their Wild Card chances are starting to slip as well. There is basically no presedent for an 0-4 team to make the playoffs, and Ladd McConkey is pretty much the only shot this team has of moving the football. Seattle has one of the league's best defenses, and the Chargers will need their top receiver to play his best football if they want to come out on top.

description: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers elevated quarterback Easton Stick and linebacker Caden Fordham from the practice squad Saturday, one day before hosting the Green Bay Packers in Week 4. fullText:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers elevated quarterback Easton Stick and linebacker Caden Fordham from the practice squad Saturday, one day before hosting the Green Bay Packers in Week 4.

Stick will back up rookie Jalon Daniels, who is set to make his NFL starting debut in place of Baker Mayfield. Mayfield dislocated his right thumb late in Tampa Bay's Week 3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings, and the Buccaneers said he is expected to miss at least three weeks.

It will snap Mayfield's streak of 57 consecutive starts for Tampa Bay, including the postseason, according to the Buccaneers.

The Packers come to Tampa at 1-2 after a rough outing in Atlanta, where they lost 35-14 on Sept. 24. Tampa Bay is still searching for its first win at 0-3.

Daniels signed with the Buccaneers as an undrafted free agent in May after six seasons at Kansas. Sports Illustrated reported that Tampa Bay named him Mayfield's backup on Aug. 30, the same weekend it released Jake Browning in final cuts.

Sunday will make him the first undrafted rookie to start a regular-season game at quarterback for the Buccaneers, according to the team.

Daniels appeared in 49 games at Kansas from 2020 to 2025. He completed 734 of 1,193 passes for 9,282 yards and 67 touchdowns. On the ground, he added 1,445 yards and 23 more scores.

Tampa Bay signed Stick to its practice squad Aug. 31. He already has some familiarity with offensive coordinator Zac Robinson's system after spending last season with Robinson in Atlanta.

The Los Angeles Chargers selected Stick in the fifth round of the 2019 NFL Draft. He has appeared in six NFL games and started four of them, completing 111 of 174 passes for 1,129 yards, three touchdowns and one interception.

This is the first practice-squad elevation of the season for both Stick and Fordham. Players can be elevated up to three times during the regular season before a team would need to sign them to the active roster to use them again. Stick and Fordham will automatically return to the practice squad after Sunday's game without going through waivers.

Fordham signed with Tampa Bay as an undrafted rookie in May and made the initial 53-man roster after cuts Aug. 30. Three days later, the Buccaneers waived him to make room for cornerback Kevin Knowles, a waiver claim from Kansas City, and brought Fordham back on the practice squad.

At North Carolina State, Fordham made 143 tackles in 2025, second in the nation. He also made his mark on special teams during the preseason, leading all NFL players with four solo tackles in kick coverage.

That could put Fordham directly into the mix Sunday. Linebacker SirVocea Dennis is questionable with a calf injury, and Buccaneers.com noted that Fordham is likely to see work in the kicking game, particularly if Dennis is unavailable.

Green Bay also adjusted its roster Saturday, placing defensive tackle Warren Brinson on injured reserve while linebacker Edgerrin Cooper cleared the concussion protocol [INTERNAL LINK: WISH Brinson IR / Cooper story, once live]. Cooper had opened the week as a limited participant because of the concussion on Green Bay's first injury report.

The Green Bay Packers placed defensive lineman Warren Brinson on the injured reserve on Saturday, just one day after they ruled him out of Week 4's action against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers with calf and groin injuries. On Friday, head coach Matt LaFleur said that Brinson, who had been battling a calf injury since warmups of Week 2 of the preseason, was injured in a non-contact fashion — leading to his groin injury — when he returned to practice this week. He said that Brinson's injury is expected to take a "significant amount of time" to recover from.

So far, Brinson hasn't been designated to return from the injured reserve. The Packers are allowed to designate eight players to return from the IR in an individual season (the number goes up to 10 if the team makes the postseason). Both receiver Savion Williams and edge defender Collin Oliver have been designated to return in 2026, while offensive tackle Zach Bako-Bewele and receiver Jayden Reed are in the Brinson camp — yet to be designated to return. PUP list players like Micah Parsons, Luke Musgrave and Jordon Riley do not count toward the IR-DFR count.

Brinson has yet to play in a regular-season game due to his calf injury, and the Packers entered the 2026 season "oversigned" at the position, as they carried seven interior defensive linemen on their initial 53-man roster — despite the team regularly rostering just five players at the position on their 48-man game-day roster.

title: ‘Redemption can’t come without genuine remorse’: NFL insider does not hold back on Deshaun Watson
description: Most of Deshaun Watson’s stint with the Cleveland Browns has been disastrous, between injuries, his poor play, and the legal issues stemming from more than 25 civil lawsuits alleging sexual misconduct during massage therapy sessions. Now, as Watson and the Browns are finally doing well on the field, one prominent NFL insider is not willing…
fullText:
Most of Deshaun Watson's stint with the Cleveland Browns has been disastrous, between injuries, his poor play, and the legal issues stemming from more than 25 civil lawsuits alleging sexual misconduct during massage therapy sessions. Now, as Watson and the Browns are finally doing well on the field, one prominent NFL insider is not willing to call it a redemption story.

After Thursday night's showdown between the Browns and the Pittsburgh Steelers, Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk called out what he saw as a "deliberate effort to boost his redemption story" regarding Watson, and he clearly was not a fan, given that Watson has never shown much remorse.

Beginning in March 2021, 24 massage therapists sued Deshaun Watson, alleging sexual misconduct during sessions while he was with the Houston Texans. Two Texas grand juries declined to indict him. By August 2022, he had settled 23 of the 24 suits.

Disciplinary officer Sue L. Robinson found a preponderance of the evidence determining that Watson had committed sexual assault, as the NFL defines it, but suspended him for just six games. The NFL appealed, and the sides settled on 11 games, a record $5 million fine, and mandatory evaluation and treatment.

In September 2024, a woman sued Watson for allegedly assaulting her on a 2020 date. He settled in October, and the NFL closed its probe in December, citing insufficient evidence. Watson has consistently denied all allegations.

Watson did offer an apology after his suspension was announced.

"I want to say that I'm truly sorry to all of the women that I have impacted in this situation," Watson said at the time. "The decisions that I made in my life that put me in this position I would definitely like to have back, but I want to continue to move forward and grow and learn and show that I am a true person of character and I am going to keep pushing forward."

However, Watson has also said multiple times since that statement that he has no regrets about his life.

Throughout Amazon Prime Video's coverage of Thursday night's game, Florio said the broadcast "featured plenty of tiptoeing around the elephant that Deshaun Watson dragged into the room with his own actions."

Florio highlighted the sit-down interview with Taylor Rooks and the periodic vague references from Al Michaels and Kirk Herbstreit to Watson's past issues as examples of the broadcast tiptoeing around Watson's self-inflicted legal issues with no direct mention of the self-created adversity Watson has experienced since 2021.

He saw the broadcast as trying to push an overall depemption narrative, with Watson finally playing well after the legal issues, injuries and on-field struggles.

"On one hand, it's a four-year-old story. On the other hand, the effects of it continue to linger. Thursday night's handling of Watson felt like a deliberate effort to boost his redemption story. But redemption can't come without genuine remorse. And the full scope of his limited comments about the incidents that derailed his career show that he has never expressed true and full and unequivocal remorse," Florio wrote for Pro Football Talk.
