fullText:
Aaron Donald's return to the NFL has been underwhelming not just for him as a player, but also for his team, the Los Angeles Rams.

They are currently third in the NFC West with a 1-2 record and will be up against the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday, October 3. However, they will be playing this game without their franchise legend Aaron Donald, who has been ruled out due to a back injury.

Head coach Sean McVay in his press conference confirmed that the player was doing well, but the team did not want to take any chances.

In two games so far, the three-time Defensive Player of the Year has not had the best of statistical output, and with the Rams losing against the Denver Broncos, criticism has started to mount on Donald.

When the Rams announced the return of Donald, many analysts named them as favourites to win the Super Bowl. He was out for the game in Australia, but returned to the line-up for their second game against the New York Giants. He looked good in that game, but was not at his best in the 30-26 loss to the Broncos.

"He's been Casper the friendly ghost, how can you be that big and be that invisible… He's had no pressures. He's like 79th out of 91 guys rushing the passer, what is going on?" said Rob Parker on Fox's The Odd Couple podcast.

"He's been a zero since he came back and now he got a back issue. He should have stayed retired, I tried to tell you this."

In the two games Donald played, he had a pressure rate of 4.8%, which ranks 79th out of 91 NFL players. This indicates that he has not started the season well, but considering he has returned after a two-year absence, some rust was expected. However, what is hurting the Rams is that they also do not have Myles Garrett, who is ruled out for 4-6 weeks due to injury.

Donald will be hoping that he finds form soon, as he returned to help the Rams get to the Super Bowl. Currently, they look far from a team that can play in February, but if Donald gets back to his former self and Garrett returns to fitness, the Rams could be the team that many believed during preseason.

title: NFL insider reveals why the Green Bay Packers remain “At least a tier below” NFL heavyweights
description: The Green Bay Packers have plenty of season left to turn things around, but their 1-2 record has put them at the bottom of the NFC North. fullText:
The Green Bay Packers have plenty of season left to turn things around, but their 1-2 record has put them at the bottom of the NFC North. Matt LaFleur's men have already dropped a divisional matchup to the 3-0 Minnesota Vikings. The team will try to even its record Sunday when it travels to face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 4.

Bleacher Report's Brad Gagnon recently summed up September for every NFL team in a single sentence. His assessment of the Green Bay Packers, however, painted a less than encouraging picture of their opening month.

"They've played three teams that didn't make the playoffs in 2025 but have yet to win a game in regulation, proving that Green Bay remains at least a tier below true heavyweight status," wrote the NFL insider.

Green Bay appeared to be in control after taking a 22-10 lead against Minnesota in the opener, but the Vikings completely took over from there. Minnesota scored 29 consecutive points to secure a 39-22 comeback victory. The Packers responded the following week by earning their first win of the year, edging the New York Jets 20-17 in overtime.

The Packers could not carry that momentum into Week 3, suffering a lopsided 35-14 defeat against the Atlanta Falcons in its home opener. The Packers struggled to slow Atlanta throughout the afternoon, allowing the Falcons to rack up nearly 500 total yards, including 242 rushing yards.

Gagnon's assessment stings because it's accurate. The Packers have faced winnable matchups and squandered opportunities, including a collapse against Minnesota and a home loss to Atlanta that revealed their defensive vulnerabilities. Heading to Tampa Bay at 1-2 adds urgency to a season that looked promising just weeks ago.

LaFleur's team can't afford another divisional-round exit, and the current trajectory suggests they're trending toward missing the playoffs entirely. The Buccaneers present a chance to salvage September, but Green Bay needs more than just one win. They need to prove they can compete with playoff contenders and execute at a consistent level.

title: Notre Dame Nabs Six Spots on Early NFL Draft Board
description: For decades, major football programs such as the Notre Dame Fighting Irish have spent heavily on training centers and experienced coaching staffs. fullText:
For decades, major football programs such as the Notre Dame Fighting Irish have spent heavily on training centers and experienced coaching staffs. Those resources help high school recruits become stronger and more prepared early in their college careers.

Top universities now run football programs that work much like professional teams. Scouts follow talented college players for years, while fans pay close attention to young players with strong physical skills.

On Thursday, sports media ESPN published its early player rankings for the 2027 professional football draft. Industry analyst Jordan Reid evaluated college athletes across the nation and selected six Notre Dame players for his top 50 list.

Leading this collegiate group, junior cornerback Leonard Moore earned the second overall spot. Reid wrote, "With excellent length, speed and technique, Moore is the prototypical cornerback prospect."

Because Moore allowed zero completed passes through late September, scouts consider him an elite defender. Furthermore, his teammate CJ Carr ranked 22nd on the national list after throwing for 963 yards and nine touchdowns.

Reid praised the young quarterback in his report, stating that Carr is a "refined pocket passer whose eyes, feet and throwing motion are always in cohesion." Consequently, Carr's accurate passing numbers elevated his status among professional evaluators.

Four additional Notre Dame athletes rounded out the prestigious board. Specifically, safety Brauntae Johnson earned the 26th position.

Subsequently, edge rusher Boubacar Traore secured spot 47 after producing 2.5 sacks this autumn. Linebacker Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa was selected 48th.

Finally, offensive lineman Anthonie Knapp grabbed the 49th rank because he surrendered only a 0.9 percent pressure rate on 230 snaps.

NFL rules require players to be at least three years removed from high school before entering the draft. True juniors and redshirt sophomores may qualify, but true freshmen and true sophomores cannot declare before completing that waiting period.

The rule prevents true college sophomores from signing NFL contracts before the 2027 draft. An early ESPN ranking gives a player attention, but it does not offer a contract or guarantee any money.

NFL teams make their own decisions during the scouting process. They study game film, conduct medical checks and watch players complete athletic drills before making draft selections.

Strong media rankings can still bring national attention to a college program. However, NFL scouts follow their own watchlists and attend practices and games based on each team's evaluation plans.

Six Notre Dame players included in early media rankings are still college students. They remain active members of the team during the current season.

title: NFL Hands Lengthy Suspension to 49ers Owner Jed York
description: The NFL has suspended San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York following his arrest for soliciting a prostitute. The post NFL Hands Lengthy Suspension to 49ers Owner Jed York appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The NFL came down hard on San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York on Friday, handing out a punishment following his arrest for soliciting a prostitute in Ohio that will no doubt leave a lasting stain on his legacy and his family's legacy as owners of 1 of the NFL's premier franchises.

"Just in: San Francisco 49ers principal owner Jed York has been suspended for six regular-season games and fined $500,000 for violating the NFL's Personal Conduct Policy," ESPN's Adam Schefter wrote on his official X account on Friday.

York was arrested on August 23 at the Wheat Hill Mobile Home Community in East Palestine, Ohio, as part of an online prostitution sting conducted by local authorities.

"Today, the NFL concluded its review, and I accept its decision in full," York said in a prepared statement. "To my family, to the players, coaches, and employees of the San Francisco 49ers, to our fans and partners, I am deeply sorry. This was an inexcusable mistake and I take full responsibility. What I did does not reflect my values or the man I strive to be for my family. While I fell short of the model I want to set for my sons, I now hope to show them the importance of owning up to one's failures, and that even our worst moments teach us to be better. Leading the 49ers is a privilege, and one I don't take lightly. Your trust will have to be earned back over time, and I look forward to that work ahead."

York has stayed away from the 49ers since his arrest and while the NFL conducted its investigation.

"49ers principal owner Jed York has been suspended for six regular-season games and fined $500,000 for violating the NFL's Personal Conduct Policy, the NFL announced today," The Ringer's Tom Pelissero wrote on his official X account on Friday. "During the time the league's investigation has been proceeding, York has stayed away from the 49ers first three regular-season games, as well as from NFL league meetings. Those three missed games are counted toward his suspension, and he may return on Tuesday, Oct. 20."

York's absence through the first 3 games of the 2026 regular season — the 49ers are 3-0 — will count toward the 6-game suspension.

"49ers owner Jed York has been suspended 6 regular-season games and fined $500,000 for violating the NFL's Personal Conduct Policy," The 33rd Team's Ari Meirov wrote on his official X account. "York was arrested after allegedly using a prostitution website to arrange a $140 sexual encounter in the summer … York was away from the team for the first 3 games of the season, and as a result that will count toward his 6-game suspension. So today's announcement is really a 3-game publicly known suspension."

fullText:
The Cleveland Browns defeated the Pittsburgh Steelers 27-24 on Thursday night, improving the team to 3-1 on the season. The Browns' early-season success has been one of the biggest surprises in the NFL this year, and it is in large part thanks to the massively improved play from veteran quarterback Deshaun Watson.

The FOX Sports Radio morning show, 2 Pros and a Cup of Joe, hosted by Brady Quinn, LaVar Arrington, and Jonas Knox, discussed the story surrounding the Browns on Friday morning.

"Credit due, hat off to (head coach Todd Monken)," Arrington said. "He has the Cleveland Browns at 3-1 after a divisional opponent in the Pittsburgh Steelers, who were coming off of a big victory over the Cincinnati Bengals. So give them credit. But I think this is honestly, potentially, this is more of an indictment on the Pittsburgh Steelers than it is a feel-good story for the Cleveland Browns.

“STOP throwing a pity party for what’s happened in the past for yourself. You won a game; make it about everyone besides YOU because, quite frankly, you’re on a really good team!”

– @Brady_Quinn on the Deshaun Watson PR spin. pic.twitter.com/Wab9BaPcmy

— FOX Sports Radio (@FoxSportsRadio) October 2, 2026

"I don't understand this need for a, well, feel-good story," Knox said. "I don't get it. What were the struggles? Let's just like break down the struggles. The struggles were: you had a fetish with the handhouse, and you weren't available. And then when you were available to play after suspension, you were injured. And then when you weren't injured, you were bad."

Quinn went on to make it clear that while he's happy for Browns' fans, he doesn't see why Deshaun Watson is throwing a "pity party" for himself.

"I feel good for the Cleveland fans. Yes. I feel good for a lot of those players," Quinn said. "I'm not sure what PR spin they're trying to put on or revisionist history they're trying to make. Anything that he endured in the past, he brought on himself. I mean, there's, there's not one part of the adversity he faced that he should have been solely responsible for.

"So like, here's the unfortunate part is we have— we're going to keep talking about this because they're going to keep bringing it up and we're going to have to keep addressing it, acknowledging it. Like, dude, stop throwing a pity party. For what's happened in the past for yourself. All right, you won a game, make it about the team, make it about everyone besides you, because quite frankly, you're on a really good team and it is about everyone besides you.

"Like, you're the quarterback, all right? This isn't Lamar Jackson in college running around carrying Louisville or at times carrying Baltimore. Like, you are there because— and you're being successful because of the help you have around you. So I just, I hope he stops with keep trying to get people to feel bad for him."

The Browns and Watson will next face the New York Jets.

title: Despite loss to Ravens, Cowboys made international NFL history in way that won’t shock anyone
description: America's team, right?
fullText:
Despite loss to Ravens, Cowboys made international NFL history in way that won't shock anyone originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

While the start of the 2026 NFL season hasn't exactly gone as planned for the Dallas Cowboys in terms of win-loss record, as Dallas currently sits at 1-2, dropping games to the New York Giants and Baltimore Ravens, there have still been some things to be somewhat happy with.

If the Cowboys can continue to play how they have against the Commanders and Ravens, mainly on the offensive side of the football, it's not unfair to say that Dallas should be one of the better teams in the NFL.

As for the fan base, everybody knows that Cowboys fans are looking for this team to win a Super Bowl.

Cowboys fans are some of the best in the world, and that's part of why the Cowboys have so much pressure to win every single season. All the fans do is show out each and every week, and that was on full display in their game against the Ravens.

According to the latest report, the Cowboys' game against the Ravens was the most-viewed international game in NFL history.

"The first regular-season NFL game held in Rio de Janeiro has set a new viewership record. The Baltimore Ravens ' 34-31 victory over the Dallas Cowboys averaged 24.9 million viewers on CBS.

"According to Nielsen data released by the network, it is the most-watched international game in NFL history," Romain Champagne of DAZN wrote.

Having a team like the Cowboys take on Lamar Jackson, and this being the most-viewed international game in NFL history, doesn't come as much of a surprise.

The Cowboys are always going to show out, and the Ravens have a great fan base themselves. Factor that in with two elite quarterbacks going at it, and if you're a fan of the NFL, you should have been watching this game. It was action-packed, though it ultimately resulted in a tough loss for Dallas, one that it likely should have felt like it could have won.

title: New biography on Ralph Wilson released
description: BUFFALO, N.Y. (WIVB) — D’Youville University hosted the release of sports historian Greg Tranter’s newest book on Thursday, ‘Ralph C. Wilson Jr., The Conscience of the NFL.
fullText:
BUFFALO, N.Y. (WIVB) -- D'Youville University hosted the release of sports historian Greg Tranter's newest book on Thursday, 'Ralph C. Wilson Jr., The Conscience of the NFL.'

The biography explores the influence of the late owner of the Buffalo Bills across 50 years in the NFL, as well as his business ventures, philanthropy, and service in World War II.

Tranter said that fans of the Bills will be fans of his book.

"It's the history of the team through his eyes, so I think they'll really like that," Tranter said. "I think they'll learn things about him that people don't know, like his military history; he was a naval guy for World War II, he spent five years in the Navy, and there's some great stories about him in the Navy, so I think they'll appreciate all that."

The book is officially on sale in local bookstores and online.

title: “It Wasn’t an Infraction”: 49ers’ Kyle Juszczyk Calls Out NFL’s Beer Endorsements After Hefty Fine for Controversial Celebration
description: Kyle Juszczyk has been celebrating on the field with a juice-chugging action for ages. However, things didn’t sit well this time, as the NFL took it as a beer chug imitation after he celebrated a touchdown pass in the game against the Miami Dolphins.
fullText:
Kyle Juszczyk has been celebrating on the field with a juice-chugging action for ages. However, things didn't sit well this time, as the NFL took it as a beer chug imitation after he celebrated a touchdown pass in the game against the Miami Dolphins. And all he did was take his right hand up to his mouth, tilt his head, and pretend to drink from the imaginary bottle.

The NFL put a $14,926 penalty on Juszczyk for the action. The San Francisco 49ers' fullback has been arguing that it was juice, not beer, in his actions. Juszczyk recently claimed that even if it was beer, the league shouldn't have put a fine on him.

"Even if it was beer, I don't think that should be a problem with all of the beer endorsements that we have in the NFL," Juszczyk told the media during a locker room interview. "We have the Bud Light Celly Can, the Bud Light Porch… We have everything. So, even if it was beer, which it wasn't, I still felt like it wasn't an infraction."

Back on December 20, 2021, Anheuser-Busch InBev, the brand behind Budweiser, signed a multi-year renewal as the global exclusive beer and hard seltzer sponsor for the league. The extension will last through the 2026-27 season.

Get the EssentiallySports Daily Newsletter. Stay ahead of the game with daily updates, exclusive stories, expert takes, and the biggest moments from the world's most popular sports.

Juszczyk further defended his case during his appearance on Jason and Travis Kelce's New Heights Podcast.

"So my nickname for the longest time has been Juice," the fullback said on the Kelce brothers' podcast. "I have literally a juice box on my thigh pad. The whole stadium yells juice when I touch the ball. So, a homage to that is literally I drink juice. And that's been going down for the longest time."

However, Travis Kelce wasn't too convinced. He claimed that the way Juszczyk did it, it looked like beer and not juice. He argued that people don't usually do a "full chug on a juice." But that invited another call for hypocrisy from the 49ers fullback.

"You can't drink juice when you got the Bud Light patio in the end zone. When you're cutting through the Bud Light celly can. It's a hypocrisy, man."

Juszczyk also noted that the NFL didn't really have to put that big of a fine on him just to make him stop doing something. He claimed that he would have stopped his celebrations had the league asked him to stop. And later, Juszczyk claimed that he doesn't drink beer.

"I don't even really drink beer," he said. "I drink maybe five times a year in the offseason, but I started thinking about it and there are two common denominators of when I do drink alcohol. One of them I was at Bandon Dunes with Travis and George. I was at Tight End U with Travis and George. And I was at Travis' wedding with Travis and George."

ESPN's Nick Wagner reported on X that Juszczyk appeared in court Tuesday to appeal the fine for "chugging a beer." As of October 1, Juszczyk is awaiting the court's decision on his appeal. However, Juszczyk believes that things will work out. Even Wagner claimed that good things will come for the 49ers fullback out of the whole situation.

Juszczyk isn't the only one facing the fines. Indianapolis Colts guard Matt Goncalves received an $8,847 fine, and the Dallas Cowboys tight end Jake Ferguson got a $13,611 fine for mimicking the consumption of a beverage that many assumed to be beer.

The NFL's decision to fine Kyle Juszczyk for drinking an imaginary beverage while heavily promoting massive beer endorsements made the fullback call out the hypocrisy. But for now, all he needs to do is wait for the court to respond to his appeal.

title: 2027 NFL Draft stock watch features 11 players on the rise
description: Who are the biggest risers in the 2027 NFL Draft so far? Two quarterbacks have helped their stock significantly with their early showings.
fullText:
As some of the marquee 2027 NFL Draft prospects have faltered in the first month of the season, other players have capitalized on the opportunity to raise their profile.

The group of prospects expected to join the pros next April features a good amount of established stars, from quarterbacks Arch Manning and Dante Moore to wide receiver Jeremiah Smith, among others. But while Smith has continued to set college football ablaze in what is almost assuredly his final campaign, the early results have been decidedly more mixed for several of his peers.

Nevertheless, September often marks the start of a steady ascent in the draft for several players. This year is no different, with a group of standouts already on the upswing.

Here's a closer look at 11 players whose early play has earned them the label of draft risers in the opening stretch of the fall:

An undersized passer who will be 25 before his rookie season and started off in Division II would typically seem like an odd figure to factor heavily into one of the most highly anticipated quarterback classes in years. Indeed, Chambliss still amounted to something of a side attraction entering this year. In continuing his full-on star turn, though, the 6-0, 208-pound passer could force teams to have some uncomfortable reconsiderations of when the circumstances are right to break from protocol and pursue an outlier. Despite playing a brutal early slate, Chambliss has racked up 12 touchdowns and carried Mississippi, proving he can excel even without Lane Kiffin's touch. Not all of his playmaking skills will translate to the NFL, but in a league where offenses place a premium on big gains, coaching staffs should covet Chambliss' calculated aggressiveness both from within and out of structure. His resiliency and decisiveness are also major strong suits. Now firmly out of range for being considered merely a developmental option or an entertaining backup, Chambliss is sure to test the creativity and adaptability of front offices as the pre-draft process continues.

Stats can hardly tell a complete story for any college quarterback, especially in a small sample size that hasn't entailed facing top competition. Still, it's impossible not to take notice of Mensah's masterful start in Miami, during which he's thrown more touchdowns (14) than incompletions (12). Exhibiting command and poise is essential for the Tulane and Duke transfer, who only has pedestrian physical tools when compared to some of the other more gifted throwers in this class. Mensah will also have to show more comfort working down the field and to the sidelines after primarily attacking short - and an understandable way to weaponize Malachi Toney - and over the middle. But if he continues to make great strides with his processing and decision-making against much firmer competition, he'll spark some compelling conversations about his placement in the quarterback pecking order.

With Baugh, Mississippi's Kewan Lacy and Missouri's Ahmad Hardy all putting forth compelling cases entering the season, the battle to be the first running back selected in 2027 figured to make for a fierce competition. Baugh, however, has seemingly cut that debate short. Through four games, he's been borderline unstoppable, rushing for a Football Bowl Subdivision-high 600 yards and 11 touchdowns. The 6-1, 225-pound ball carrier already had all the trappings of a workhorse back. This fall, though, he's ripped off a run of 50 yards or 

Chambliss might be the catalyst for Mississippi's attack, but electric pass catchers are required to make the most of the quarterback's daring tendencies. Having risen from an integral part of a robust receiver room to the focal point of the passing attack, Alexander is more than doing his part to make good on Chambliss' deep-ball prowess. The former Wake Forest transfer has racked up 429 yards - the second most in the Southeastern Conference - and four touchdowns in four games. His background as a high school track standout in Georgia is readily evident on every snap, as he's particularly adept at getting corners to bite at the faintest sign of a fake or hesitation before racing past them downfield. The 6-0, 180-pound target might need to fill out his frame a bit more and demonstrate he can consistently conquer press coverage, but his game-breaking potential should have him rocketing up draft boards.

With Jordyn Tyson off to the Saints, the Sun Devils reloaded at receiver by inking two major transfers in Harris and Omarion Miller. The latter figured to be the more consequential move for next year's draft, but the former is making a far bigger splash early in the season. Harris has accounted for 374 receiving yards - nearly half of his team's total output - along with five touchdown catches. His deep-threat credentials had already been established at Boston College, but the 6-5, 220-pound pass catcher is reinforcing his field-stretching skills by averaging 17.4 yards per reception. In a receiver class that lacks much clarity beyond the top trio of Smith, Coleman and Becker, Harris has mounted a push for a spot in the top 50 - and possibly consideration even earlier.

Does college football have a sufficient supply of talented tight ends to satisfy the NFL's uptick in demand at the position? Beyond Oregon's Jamari Johnson and LSU's Trey'Dez Green, this year's group doesn't seem to measure up to the one teams flocked to in April. The emergence of Reynolds, however, has helped quell some concerns about depth in the upcoming draft. As one of a horde of former Penn State players who followed James Franklin to Virginia Tech, the former five-star recruit has found his footing in a new setting, needing just four games to set career highs with 30 catches, 280 yards and four touchdowns. The 6-4, 250-pound target can't measure up to Johnson or Green as an athletic marvel, but he's nimble enough to free himself from coverage and pick up additional yards after the catch. And with his comfort working as an inline blocker, Reynolds should be an attractive option for a team looking to round out and diversify its offense.

With bookend offensive tackles Francis Mauigoa and Markel Bell both departing as early NFL draft picks, Miami could have been forgiven if it struggled with pass protection in the early going this season. Okunlola ensured that didn't happen. The 6-6, 330-pound blocker stepped in at left tackle and has been superlative from the start, helping keep Mensah as part of a front that has allowed just three total sacks on 136 total dropbacks thus far. Some more refinement would serve the first-year starter well, but a former five-star recruit who was nicknamed "The Pancake Honcho" shouldn't require a hard sell for teams if he keeps playing like this.

Put Johnson anywhere along the front and he's bound to excel. The third-year starter has played at every spot except right guard during his time at Minnesota and made another switch last week, moving back to center from left guard. The result: The 6-6, 325-pound blocker was named the Outland Trophy National Player of the Week. Though his best work has come as a forceful presence in the ground game, Johnson has also helped put statuesque pocket passer Drake Lindsey at ease. Considered by some as a fringe first-round prospect entering the year - he checked in at No. 28 to the Bills in my preseason mock draft - Johnson now might be firmly in Day 1 territory.

It should come as little surprise that a former basketball standout who played just one year of high school football might need some time before fully coming into his own against top college competition. Thompkins showed promise in stretches in 2024-25 after playing in just three games during his first two years at USC, but he's taken his game to a distinct new level after transferring to Alabama. Through four games, he's already matched his previous career high with three sacks on the season. Thompkins is far more nimble and explosive than one might expect of a 6-5, 300-pound defensive linemen. He might not be a fit for every team given his body type and skill set, but he could be a considerably disruptive force as a 3-4 defensive end or defensive tackle in a defense that allows him to get upfield.

With offenses across the NFL shifting back to more under-center looks, it might not be long before teams scramble to add hyperathletic linebackers as a necessary countermeasure for the schematic swing. Cole might be exactly what those defenses are in search of. The 6-3, 235-pounder already demonstrated his ample pursuit speed and bend last season, when he led the Bulldogs with 4 1/2 sacks as a backup. Now, however, he's getting to showcase the full extent of his abilities, as his size and fluidity allow him to stick with running backs and tight ends in coverage or chase down ball carriers to either sideline. He also served up a reminder of just how uniquely explosive he is for his position when he scooped up Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer's fumble and raced 85 yards to the end zone with it, pulling away from his opponents like a wide receiver breaking free from an overmatched corner.

In snagging five interceptions in his first three games, Lopa, the 6-5, 210-pound safety, has stepped to the forefront as one of college football's most scintillating young defensive playmakers. The Oregon transfer is still in need of some seasoning after playing sparingly in his first two years with the Ducks. His tackling, in particular, isn't yet up to par, as he can struggle when forced to come to balance and finish off plays even when he's in position to do so. fullText:
Justin Jefferson is arguably the best wide receiver in the NFL, but the former first-round pick suffered an ankle injury against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and could not return to the game. The fifth wide receiver taken in the 2025 NFL Draft, Justin Jefferson quickly established himself as one of the biggest steals in his draft class. Appearing in all 16 games while making 14 starts, the rookie finished his inaugural campaign with 88 receptions for 1,400 yards and seven touchdowns.

He continued to dominate from there, earning First-Team All-Pro honors on two separate occasions while leading the league in receptions (128) and yards (1,809) in 2022. The 2025 season was a relative down year as he struggled to develop a rapport with quarterback J.J. McCarthy, but he still ended the season with 84 receptions for 1,048 yards and two touchdowns. While Justin Jefferson looked like his old self in the first two weeks of the season, he suffered an ankle injury early in Week 3 and could not return to the field. While this won't be a long-term injury, the superstar wideout did not practice yesterday and could miss Week 4's contest against the Miami Dolphins.

It's hard to overstate just how unfortunate a serious Justin Jefferson injury would be for the Minnesota Vikings, and how lucky the team is that this isn't a long-term issue. Even with the star wide receiver in the lineup, Minnesota's passing attack hasn't looked all too dominant thus far in the season. Starting quarterback Kyler Murray suffered a concussion early in Week 1, forcing journeyman Carson Wentz to finish the contest and start Week 2. While Murray returned to the lineup in Week 3, he didn't look all too impressive. Playing most of the contest without Justin Jefferson, the quarterback completed just 15 of his 29 attempts for 168 yards, one touchdown, and one interception.

The Minnesota Vikings are a worse team without Justin Jefferson in the lineup, but they probably won't need him to win in Week 4. The Miami Dolphins are perhaps the worst team in football, and Jefferson probably won't be the difference between a win and a loss. There is no such thing as an easy win in the NFL, but Minnesota is considerably more talented and should comfortably win this contest.

title: NFL apparently told Rams that pass interference penalty on Josh Wallace shouldn't have been called late in loss to Broncos
description: A questionable pass interference call negated a late interception and helped the Broncos beat the Rams on Sunday night.
fullText:
Josh Wallace should not have been called for pass interference on Sunday night in Denver.

That's what Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay said he was told by the league in the wake of their 30-26 loss to the Broncos, which was partially decided by the penalty on Wallace in the final minutes of that contest.

Wallace appeared to intercept a pass from Broncos quarterback Bo Nix late on Sunday, but he was instead called for pass interference. That negated the interception and set up a first-and-goal for the Broncos, which eventually led to their go-ahead touchdown and the SCORE win.

While it looked as if Wallace committed the penalty in real time, a closer look undoubtedly put that call into question. Even NBC rules analyst Terry McAulay thought it shouldn't have been called.

NBC rules analyst Terry McAulay did not believe Rams CB Josh Wallace should have been flagged for pass interference, in what may have otherwise been an interception. 

The Broncos went on to score what would serve as the game-winning TD. pic.twitter.com/A0YDJ8ZmZl

Had Wallace been granted the interception, the Rams would have gotten the ball back on their own 8-yard line leading 26-23 with 69 seconds left in the game. The Broncos did have three timeouts still, and could have gotten the ball back, but the interception would have absolutely put the Rams in position to seal the game.

Instead, the Broncos scored and held on to grab the win.

"[It] doesn't really matter," McVay said about the call on Monday. "It is what it is. That was the call that was made and there was a lot of opportunities that we had to be able to close the door on that game. ... But I wouldn't have any additional coaching points for how Josh [Wallace] plays through the cycle of the snap. But I'm not going to make excuses either and we're not going to play the victim card."

Though McVay was the one who revealed that the league told him it shouldn't have been called, his comments from Monday still stand. As it is several days later, the penalty stands as called. The Rams lost the game, and fell to 1-2 on the season.

The errant call, as the league or officials didn't step in to reverse it in real time, stands and the season moves on.

The message on the No. 87 jersey called Bowe a brother forever and said he showed Kelce how to be a pro. It also named him one of the realest on and off the field, and added a nod to Kelce's new record for most yards after the catch.

The strong form carried into Week 3. Kelce opened the Dolphins game with a 48-yard catch and run, then caught an 11-yard touchdown from Mahomes with 2:55 left. He ended with two catches for 59 yards as the Chiefs improved to 3-0.

At 36, he returned on a one-year deal after months of retirement talk, and he now looks like a key piece of Kansas City's offense.

title: Keenum stars for Bears on first start since 2023
description: Veteran quarterback Case Keenum throws for two touchdowns and rushes for another as the Chicago Bears beat the Philadelphia Eagles in the NFL.
fullText:
Veteran quarterback Case Keenum starred on his first start for almost three years as the Chicago Bears handed the Philadelphia Eagles their first defeat of the season.

Starting his first NFL game since December 2023, the 38-year-old threw for 247 yards and two touchdowns and rushed for another as the Bears won 27-7 at Soldier Field in Chicago.

It is the first time he has thrown multiple touchdowns in a game since October 2019, while he is also the oldest player to score a rushing touchdown for the Bears.

Third-choice quarterback Keenum, an NFL journeyman playing at his eighth franchise, was called into action because Caleb Williams suffered a hamstring injury last week and his back-up Tyson Bagent then suffered a concussion.

Wide receiver Kalif Raymond, who scored a touchdown, said: "He was like, 'I may not be a cowboy, but this is definitely not my first rodeo'. [There's] a lot of confidence in him; a lot of confidence in himself.

"He practises, preps every week, but particularly this week. We didn't expect anything different from him."

Keenum's first drive resulted in a touchdown for Luther Burden III, and Cairo Santos added a 29-yard field goal before Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts rushed for a touchdown to cut the Bears' half-time lead to 10-7.

Santos added a second field goal early in the third quarter before the Bears scored two touchdowns among 17 unanswered points.

The Bears defence limited the Eagles to 248 total yards and claimed two interceptions - one from Jalen Hurts and another from his back-up Andy Dalton, who came in for four snaps while Hurts was checked for a potential concussion in the second quarter.

title: NFL power rankings: Nick’s picks for how teams stack up before Week 4
description: Nick’s NFL power rankings heading into Week 4
fullText:
Somehow, the Buffalo Bills turned the football over five times and still WON THE GAME! Of course, it was against the Chargers, who are currently — and historically — allergic to winning, but James Cook's 154 yards on the ground helped give Buffalo the 24-16 win, and they remain at the top of the standings here.

Brock Purdy and the 49ers are one of the hottest teams in football. Purdy went for 297 yards and four touchdowns against an inferior Cardinals team, who pushed the 49ers in the 36-30 game. Still, through all the injuries, the 49ers remain a top team in the NFL.

The Chiefs went into Miami and easily handled the Dolphins. Patrick Mahomes was efficient (20 of 24 for 246 yards with two touchdowns), and Rashee Rice finally got going with seven catches for 88 yards. Miami offered little resistance in the 24-10 win, and the Chiefs are one of the four undefeated teams that remain in the NFL.

Seattle goy Sam Darnold back from his hip injury, but Washington did an excellent job harrassing the Seahawks all game. Darnold finished with 379 passing yards and four touchdowns, but Marcus Mariota did enough to give the Commanders a 33-31 home victory.

The Rams drop to 1-2 but remain in the top five. Massive credit to the Broncos, who appeared dead for much of the game but battled back with 30 second-half points. Matt Stafford finished with 390 yards passing and two touchdowns, but the Rams' game plan shifted after a Terrance Ferguson injury, and they were without Puka Nukua, who they hope will return soon.

Tyler Loop! The Ravens and Dallas were headed to overtime after Dak Prescott led the Cowboys down the field on a last-minute drive to tie the game with a field goal. Unfortunately for Dallas, Lamar Jackson found Zay Flowers for 27 yards, which set up a 56-yarder from Loop for a big road victory over Jerry Jones' Cowboys.

The Vikings have moved eight spots up in the rankings over the last two weeks. They're undefeated, but sit seventh in the rankings; this is because of my discomfort with Kyler Murray, who missed Week 2 with a concussion. The Vikings' defense, led by Brian Flores, is playing amazing football, and they beat up on the Buccaneers, 23-16. Still, the offense isn't going to be bailed out by the strong defense every week; the team must become more complementary.

The Broncos defeated a very good Rams team at home with second-half resilience. The win was similar to their win over the Giants last year, where they scored 30 points in the fourth quarter; they did that in the second half, and the Broncos' defense slowed down Matt Stafford when it mattered most.

Chicago dismantled the Philadelphia Eagles with 38-year -old journeyman quarterback Case Keenum. Ben Johnson continues to prove why he's an offensive wizard, and he unlocked the potential of Luther Burden III in the game. Kalif Raymond finished with six grabs for 90 yards and a touchdown, as Philadelphia was held to seven points and 248 total yards. Impressive win against a struggling, now 2-1 Eagles team.

The Bengals gave up 292 yards and three touchdowns to Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers. After two strong weeks of defensive football, the Bengals' defense struggled to stop Ja'Marr Chase (9 catches for 98 yards and a touchdown) and Jaylen Warren, who rushed for 127 yards. Cincinnati will be okay, but this was a tough loss.

The New England Patriots are spiraling right now, and Jacksonville took advantage of that fact in Week 3. Jacksonville beat up on the Patriots, 35-6, with Drake Maye looking very bad, finishing 14 of 25 for 199 yards with a pair of interceptions. Jacksonville got back on track against the AFC champs from last season.

Detroit was pushed by the New York Jets, but they found a way to win late in the 31-24 game against a feisty Jets team. Jaymeir Gibbs finished with 99 yards and a pair of touchdowns on 20 carries, and the Lions sit at 2-1.

The Eagles are a 2-1 team that does not inspire much hope. Jalen Hurts still has his flaws as a passer, and they were just embarrassed in primetime by the Chicago Bears. Things do not get much easier for the Eagles, as they host the Rams next Sunday and then travel to London to play the Jaguars.

The Raiders are undefeated! And they just went into a hostile New Orleans environment and defeated the Saints 35-21. Brock Bowers' return was exciting, as the young tight end caught 10 passes for 116 yards and a touchdown. Kirk Cousins is doing enough to put the Raiders into advantageous situations, as they sit undefeated.

I hate having the 1-2 Dallas Cowboys this high, especially with their suspect defense through three weeks. But I know how explosive their offense can be with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. Plus, their rushing attack is getting going, and they'll be getting Tyler Smith back soon. The defense remains an issue, of course, but Dallas stays put at 14.

I didn't expect to see Aaron Rodgers dial back the clock against a Bengals defense that tormented the Buccaneers and Texans in their first two matchups. The Steelers' defense remains their strength, but competent quarterback play makes them a threat, so they are in the top-fifteen.

The Colts finally got their first victory against the Houston Texans on a last-second field goal. Indianapolis struggled to do much against a very good Texans defense, but they found a way to get a valuable win and send the Texans to 0-3.

I don't like having the 0-3 Texans this high, but I feel better about their position — specifically with their defense — than I do with the remaining teams, including the injured Giants, so here we are. Houston pushed Buffalo and the Colts to near victories; they must get more out of their offense and learn to secure wins, but they're better than their 0-3 record would indicate.

The Giants are 2-1 and handled their business in a sloppy noreaster against the Tennessee Titans. New York has issues with Jameis Winston; the trade for J.J. McCarthy may eventually solve that problem, but the Giants are beat up on both sides of the ball. However, Jordan Stout is a stud. The Giants can still compete for this NFC East with their current injury situation, and I expect better play out of Jameis Winston, although I'm relieved they'll have another viable option.

Washington pulled off one of the season's more impressive wins, defeating the Super Bowl champions 33-31 at home. Perhaps it was Sam Darnold jitters, or the dreaded one-o-clock start for a West Coast team — I'm not sure — but it does seem like Washington's defense has improved, and Marcus Mariota did enough against Mike Macdonald's talented defense

Las Vegas just might be a much better football team than many anticipated, and the Saints found that out firsthand. Tyler Shough played well, throwing four touchdowns with 255 yards passing. Still, the Raiders forced four turnovers and the Saints lost running back Travis Etienne to injury. New Orleans is a quality 1-2 team, but they're still young and learning themselves.

The Panthers suffered a tough loss to the now 2-1 Browns. Bryce Young threw for 291 yards and one touchdown in the 21-18 loss, but the Dawg Pound did enough to earn DeShaun Watson his first home win in years.

The New York Jets are the SECOND-rated team in the NFC East. They've lost their last two, but were in both games and have looked competent on offense with Geno Smith. They're exceeding expectations and have been solid defensively. The Jets are no longer a doormat in the NFL.

Look, the Browns are 2-1. Watson finished with 144 passing yards and a pair of passing touchdowns in a slow-paced win against the Panthers. I don't think the Browns are a legitimate contender in the AFC North, but they beat two NFC South teams and have looked better than I expected, which is something.

The Falcons just beat up on the Green Bay Packers in Wisconsin, 35-14. Green Bay rushed for 17 yards at home as favorites on Thursday Night Football — great job by Atlanta's defense. The return of Michael Penix proved to be just what Atlanta needed. We'll see if they can continue to stack wins with help from talented play-makers like Bijan Robinson and Drake London.

Arizona pushed San Francisco in the 30-36 loss. They leaned on Jeremiyah Love, who had 21 carries for 90 yards, while Jacoby Brissett tossed 52 passes for 280 yards and a pair of touchdowns. The Cardinals are better than expected, but are still a team that could use an upgrade in personnel.

Yes — what a fall for the Patriots! There is no more excusing it — THEYYYYY STINK! New England is all sorts of messed up on offense, and Drake Maye has looked lost through three games. Their offensive line is injured and hasn't played well and no receivers can create separation. It's a tough watch for the defending Super Bowl champions.

The Packers were embarrassed at home against the Falcons. Green Bay, much like the Patriots and the next team we'll discuss, looked lost offensively, and Jordan Love is the only reason they have not imploded. They can't run the ball at all, and their offense is completely one-dimensional.

Only the Chargers can lose a game when their opponent turns the ball over five times. Justin Herbert's late interception was terrible and this offense is playing horribly. Omarion Hampton doesn't appear to be a fit for Mike McDaniel's scheme, which has looked bad with this personnel. It's full-on panic in Los Angeles for the Chargers.

The Buccaneers are winless, and Baker Mayfield just suffered a hand injury. They, at least, weren't embarrassed against the Vikings, but still picked up the L.

Tennessee lost to the Giants in a monsoon. Cam Ward struggled, but the Titans' defense was solid against Jameis Winston and the Giants' heavy rushing attack. The Titans are young, but have been competitive in their last two games. Still, they're a bottom team in the NFL.

Miami lost to the Kansas City Chiefs and De'Von Achane suffered a torn ACL. Again, it's going to be a very long year for the Dolphins.

title: Bears’ quarterback plan for Jets remains unsettled despite Case Keenum’s big night

fullText:
Case Keenum threw for 247 yards and two touchdowns and scored on a goal-line sneak in the Chicago Bears' 27-7 win over the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday night, his first NFL start since Dec. 24, 2023. Ben Johnson still would not commit to him for Sunday.

Caleb Williams is highly unlikely to be back from a Grade 2 hamstring strain when the New York Jets visit Soldier Field on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET. That leaves Johnson choosing between Keenum and Tyson Bagent on a six-day turnaround.

"We'll have a discussion as a coaching staff and we'll see where we need to go from here," Johnson said. "There was a reason why Tyson ended training camp as our No. 2 quarterback."

That seems to lean toward Bagent, who finished camp ahead of Keenum, the Bears' third-stringer when the season opened. Keenum's night makes the call harder than it looked a week ago. He completed 24 of 34 passes for a 110.8 passer rating, and Chicago's defense forced three takeaways and held Philadelphia to seven points in a win that moved the Bears to sixth in Sports Fountain's Week 3 top 10.

Johnson used a similar line on Saturday, the Chicago Sun-Times noted, and later said he was fairly set on starting Keenum by that point. Johnson has also described the Eagles call as an easy one, citing how convincing Keenum was in practice. Treating Monday's answer as a decision would ignore how he handled the same question two days before kickoff.

Ben Johnson when asked who will start next week at QB:

There is a reason Tyson ended training camp as our number 2 QB.

Obviously nothing concrete but from the sounds of that seems like Tyson will be the starter next week. #Bears #DaBears pic.twitter.com/BO4cGndupm

— Clay Harbor (@clayharbs82) September 29, 2026

Bagent entered the concussion protocol after playing the final two drives of the Week 2 loss to Minnesota, missed the first two practices of the week and was not cleared until Sunday morning. Keenum took the starting reps and the game plan was built around him. Bagent is healthy this week, so the preparation problem that decided Monday's start has gone away.

Bagent is 2-2 as a starter, with all four of those games coming as an undrafted rookie in 2023. Keenum, 38, had gone 1,009 days without a start, and his main job over the last two seasons was mentoring Williams and Bagent. He also had help, as Philadelphia opened the second half with three straight three-and-outs and gained seven yards on those nine plays.

Williams was hurt on Sept. 20, and the three-to-four-week estimate on his strain points to a return somewhere between the Oct. 11 trip to Green Bay and the Oct. 18 game in Atlanta. Whoever starts against the Jets may only be holding the job for one or two weeks.

description: Second-year NFL quarterback J.J. McCarthy was traded on Monday by Minnesota to the New York Giants, hoping to boost their scoring after a season-ending injury to starting signal-caller Jaxson Dart. The Vikings received a fifth-round pick in next year's NFL Draft for McCarthy, who was selected 10th overall in the 2024 draft but missed the 2024 season with a right knee injury.
fullText:
Second-year NFL quarterback J.J. McCarthy was traded on Monday by Minnesota to the New York Giants, hoping to boost their scoring after a season-ending injury to starting signal-caller Jaxson Dart.

The Vikings received a fifth-round pick in next year's NFL Draft for McCarthy, who was selected 10th overall in the 2024 draft but missed the 2024 season with a right knee injury.

"Really glad, really happy, very excited to add J.J. McCarthy. Think he's a strong young quarterback," said Giants coach John Harbaugh.

"Has some experience in National Football League, obviously was a very high draft pick, very talented player, and is going to make us a stronger football team."

Dart suffered a left knee injury a week ago early in a 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams and his replacement, Jameis Winston, struggled in a 12-7 victory over Tennessee last Sunday.

John Harbaugh knows well 23-year-old McCarthy, who played in college at Michigan under Harbaugh's brother Jim, now coach of the Los Angeles Chargers.

"We've been turning over every stone. This was an opportunity that came up. And able to finish the deal off this morning, late morning," said Harbaugh.

However, Harbaugh told reporters that Winston will start the Giants' next game against the Arizona Cardinals this Sunday, and will remain his starting quarterback "as long as I can see into the future."

He indicated that McCarthy will require time to "get to work on learning the offense."

The coach also defended Winston's performance against the Titans on Sunday, noting the quick turnaround from the Giants' previous Monday night game, and the stormy "nor'easter" conditions in which the game in New Jersey was played.

"We'll be ready to play this next game, and going forward, excited about Jameis," he said.

McCarthy went 6-4 last season as a starter for Minnesota, completing 140-of-243 passes for 1,632 yards and 11 touchdowns with 12 interceptions. He also ran for 181 yards and four touchdowns.

McCarthy, however, became expendable this season. He lost his starting role this season to free agent signing Kyler Murray, who went into concussion protocol and was replaced by Carson Wentz, who filled in until Murray returned in a 23-16 victory at Tampa Bay for the 3-0 Vikings.

Minnesota saves $4.5 million in salary cap space with the move.

Former NFL player Emmanuel Acho criticized the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' decision-making after Baker Mayfield suffered an injury during a costly sequence against the Minnesota Vikings. Acho questioned the choice to attempt a fourth-and-13 from Tampa Bay's own 39-yard line, a decision that ended with an interception and Mayfield getting hurt on the play.

The Buccaneers entered the situation trailing by four points but still had all three timeouts available. Instead of punting and forcing Minnesota's struggling offense to drive the length of the field, Tampa Bay elected to keep its offense on the field for a difficult fourth-down conversion attempt.

The decision carried significant risk given the field position and distance needed for a first down. Mayfield dropped back and attempted to make a play, but the possession ended with an interception, turning an aggressive decision into a major setback for a team already searching for answers.

The consequences became even more concerning when Mayfield was injured during the sequence. The quarterback suffered a dislocated thumb on his throwing hand, adding another layer of uncertainty to a Buccaneers team that had already endured a difficult start to the season.

Acho shared his thoughts about how Tampa Bays' coaching led to Mayfield's injury. This can be seen in a post he made on his official X account.

There’s some really idiotic coaching in the NFL—

The Buccaneers have 3 timeouts and are at their own 39, down by 4. They decide to go for it on 4th and 13 as opposed to punting it to a struggling Kyler Murray.

The play results in Mayfield hurt after throwing an interception.

— Emmanuel Acho (@EmmanuelAcho) September 27, 2026

Acho's reaction focused on the coaching decision rather than simply the turnover or injury itself. His criticism centered on the opportunity Tampa Bay had to punt, rely on its defense and put pressure on Minnesota's offense, particularly with the Vikings' quarterback struggling to generate consistent production.

The sequence ultimately became a defining moment in another frustrating afternoon for Tampa Bay. The fourth-down gamble failed to produce the needed conversion, Mayfield left the play injured and the Buccaneers were left to deal with both the immediate consequences and questions about the decision that created such a high-risk situation.

Matthew Stafford made NFL history for an unwanted reason as the Los Angeles Rams suffered a stunning 30-26 loss to the Denver Broncos. The veteran quarterback threw his 33rd career pick-six, surpassing Brett Favre for the most in league history.

The record-breaking play came with the Rams holding a 19-16 lead in the fourth quarter. Talanoa Hufanga jumped in front of a pass intended for Kyren Williams and returned the interception 66 yards for a touchdown, giving Denver its first lead of the night.

The mistake was particularly costly because Los Angeles had controlled much of the game early. The Rams carried a 16-0 advantage into halftime before the Broncos mounted a second-half comeback, turning the contest into a back-and-forth battle that remained undecided until the final seconds.

Stafford did not allow the interception to derail him immediately, responding with a 48-yard touchdown pass to Konata Mumpfield on the next possession. That score put Los Angeles back in front 26-23, demonstrating how quickly the veteran quarterback could recover from a major mistake and keep his team within striking distance.

Stafford recently made unwanted history as his team lost to the Broncos this week. This can be seen in a post shared by NFL Researcher on X.

title: Broncos deny Rams and Seahawks lose - five things from NFL week three
description: The NFL produced another thrilling day of action with a shock for the defending Super Bowl champions and several tight finishes.
fullText:
The NFL produced another thrilling day of action on Sunday with a shock for the defending champions as five teams maintained their unbeaten record this season.

There were several nail-biting finishes as 12 of the 14 games were decided by eight points or fewer, tying the NFL record for the most one-score games in a day.

One of those took place in Brazil, where the NFL staged the second of a record nine international games to be played this season.

But they saved the best for last as the two teams that went within one win of last season's Super Bowl traded blows in a gripping primetime clash.

The Denver Broncos and the Los Angeles Rams remain potential Super Bowl contenders after losing last season's Conference Championship games.

Both teams had an underwhelming season opener before bouncing back last week, and Sunday's game in Denver gave them an opportunity to show their title credentials.

The Rams dominated the first half and led 16-0 at the interval, but the Broncos regrouped to draw level in the third quarter.

That set up a fascinating finish, with three lead changes in the final five minutes, beginning with an interception by Denver safety Talanoa Hufanga which he ran back for a 66-yard touchdown.

In just over a minute, last season's Most Valuable Player Matt Stafford led the Rams down the field, culminating in a 48-yard touchdown for receiver Konata Mumpfield to regain the lead.

The Broncos replied with quarterback Bo Nix reaching into the endzone after another long drive to put the hosts back in front.

That left Stafford 47 seconds to get into a game-winning position and he did just that. With two seconds left, he had a shot at the endzone from 19 yards, but Hufanga intercepted for a second time to clinch a 30-26 Broncos win.

The Washington Commanders' hopes of getting back in the play-offs were dealt a huge blow last week as quarterback Jayden Daniels dislocated his left elbow.

But Daniels could be back inside three weeks and, although the Commanders hosted defending champions the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday, they led 24-10 after experienced back-up Marcus Mariota threw his third touchdown pass.

The Seahawks drew level in the fourth quarter, but Sam Darnold, who returned from a game out for Seattle, then threw his second interception, and it was returned by linebacker Kain Medrano for a 50-yard score.

That proved enough for Washington to clinch a 33-31 win and halt a 12-game win streak by Seattle, which included last season's Super Bowl run.

The New England Patriots were their opponents in the Super Bowl, but their quarterback Drake Maye has struggled since.

After having only 11 turnovers last year, he already has seven this season after another three against the Jacksonville Jaguars, and he was benched as the Jags romped to a 35-6 home win.

After playing in Sao Paulo the past two seasons, the NFL returned to Brazil for its first game in Rio de Janeiro.

There had been concerns about the condition of the field at the iconic Maracana stadium, but there were no issues.

The NFL picked a mouth-watering match-up for Rio and it delivered, with the Baltimore Ravens and the Dallas Cowboys producing a thriller.

Two Derrick Henry touchdowns helped the Ravens into a 24-13 lead in the third quarter before Dallas, playing only their second international game, fought back.

The lead changed hands twice in the fourth quarter and the game looked set for overtime when a Cowboys field goal levelled the score with seven seconds left.

But Lamar Jackson then completed a 27-yard pass down the middle to get the Ravens within field-goal range and Tyler Loop made a 56-yard kick as time expired to win the game 34-31.

That sparked wild celebrations at the Maracana and means all four AFC North teams have a 2-1 record this season.

Some Cleveland Browns fans cheered when quarterback Deshaun Watson suffered a season-ending injury in 2024.

Some booed as he returned to action in pre-season, but could Watson finally be winning over the 'Dawg Pound'?

The 31-year-old led the Browns to a comeback win at the Tampa Bay Buccaneers last week and repeated the feat as Cleveland beat the Carolina Panthers 21-18 in their home opener.

Watson held his nerve to step out of the pocket and fire a 14-yard touchdown pass to tight end Harold Fannin Jr to cap a game-winning 65-yard drive.

"The past is the past," said Watson. "I know we've been through some ups and downs. But if we look forward, build off this win, come back Thursday night and get another big one, we can make something special for this city."

The Browns are at home again on Thursday against divisional rivals the Pittsburgh Steelers, who enjoyed a morale-boosting victory in another AFC North match-up on Sunday.

After only one offensive touchdown in their opening two games, Aaron Rodgers got the Steelers firing, throwing three touchdown passes before Derrick Harmon pulled off a strip-sack on Joe Burrow to seal a 30-27 win at home to the Cincinnati Bengals.

Three of the teams who remain unbeaten are regular play-off contenders. The Buffalo Bills came from 10-0 down to beat the Los Angeles Chargers 24-16, with quarterback Josh Allen barging over for two touchdowns.

Travis Kelce scored as the Kansas City Chiefs won 24-10 at the Miami Dolphins, while Brock Purdy threw four touchdown passes in the San Francisco 49ers' 36-30 win at home to the Arizona Cardinals.

Few expected the Minnesota Vikings to be 3-0, though. They won 23-16 at Tampa Bay despite losing receiver Justin Jefferson to an early ankle injury.

And the biggest surprise has been the Las Vegas Raiders. They have now won as many games as they did last season, when they had the league's worst record.

For the third straight game veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins threw for three touchdowns as the Raiders fought back from 27-16 down to win 35-27 at the New Orleans Saints.

The Philadelphia Eagles could make it six teams with a 3-0 record when they end week three with a trip to the Chicago Bears on Monday.

title: 32 things we learned in NFL Week 3: Bills don't look good, literally or figuratively
description: Every season, the team's winless and undefeated teams draw a lot of scrutiny after two weeks – uet that script tends to flip, as it did Sunday in Washington.
fullText:
The 32 things we learned from Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season:

0(-3). That would be a reference to the league's winless teams, of which there are five (Houston Texans, Miami Dolphins, Los Angeles Chargers, Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Tennessee Titans) now saddled with that weighty record − one only seven teams in league history have overcome to make the playoffs. The Texans managed to do it in 2025, but no club has ever pulled it off in successive seasons. (But worth noting that Houston is the only team in the 21st century to surmount the 0-3 challenge, also pulling it off in 2018.)

1. Back to that familiar question that's pervaded the early part of the 2026 season: Who's No. 1? It's now a tough case to make for the reigning champion Seattle Seahawks after they lost at Washington to a team without its starting quarterback. The Buffalo Bills were fortunate to survive the winless Chargers, QB Josh Allen playing a terrible game in a terrible uniform … more on those fronts later. The undefeated San Francisco 49ers? Can they field a functional team next week? Ready to make a case for the Las Vegas Raiders or Minnesota Vikings, who are also 3-0? Ready to re-anoint the dynastic Kansas City Chiefs ... despite a fairly ugly win at feckless Miami? Check nfl.usatoday.com on Tuesday morning once the dust has fully settled … and our next batch of power rankings are out of the oven.

1a. Prior to Sunday's game against the Baltimore Ravens in Rio de Janeiro, the Dallas Cowboys had appeared in one international game – the fewest in NFL history. But they may have also participated in the best international game in league history. Keep reading ...

(QB)2: Kudos to backups Marcus Mariota and Jameis Winston, who led the Commanders and New York Giants, respectively, to wins Sunday – a week after both teams lost their starting quarterbacks, the Giants' Jaxson Dart expected to miss the rest of the season. Next up? Chicago Bears veteran backup Case Keenum, who is expected to start Monday night against the Philadelphia Eagles in place of injured Caleb Williams.

3(-0). Five teams currently sport that spotless record (49ers, Bills, Chiefs, Raiders and Vikings). Philly can join their ranks Monday night with a win at Soldier Field.

4. The number of consecutive seasons an 0-2 team knocked off a 2-0 team, which happened Sunday when the Commanders ambushed the Seahawks, who won 38-14 at Northwest Stadium last November. And the upset came amid Seattle QB Sam Darnold's return from his Week 1 gluteal injury − and he played his butt off Sunday with 379 yards and four TDs through the air.

5. The number of turnovers committed by the Bills on Sunday, three courtesy of Allen. It was Buffalo's first win with that many giveaways since 1997. Good thing Buffalo's defense finally showed up, even if the Bolts offense didn't ... again.

5a. Ugly a game as he had, Allen became the first QB in NFL history with multiple rushing TDs in three consecutive games.

6. The number of TD receptions by Seahawks WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who's excelling, per usual, no matter which of his quarterbacks is throwing to him. The 2025 Offensive Player of the Year is on a very early pace to shatter Hall of Famer Randy Moss' single-season record (23 TD grabs in 2007).

Jaxon Smith-Njigba has had 120+ receiving yards and 1+ receiving TD in each of his team's first 3 games 🫨

The only other player to accomplish that in NFL history is HOF Jerry Rice@Seahawks | #GoHawks pic.twitter.com/nVNt719IkI

7. However it appears the Detroit Lions' Jahmyr Gibbs is going to give JSN a run for his money when it comes to capturing 2026 OPOY honors. Gibbs, who posted 164 yards and three touchdowns from scrimmage in Sunday's 31-24 defeat of the New York Jets, is off to a historic start.

.@Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs is the first player in @NFL history to produce the following statistics through the first 3 games of any season:

- 300 rushing yards
- 4 rushing TDs
- 150 receiving yards
- 2 receiving TDs#OnePride pic.twitter.com/YGj3AZSIMe

8. The jersey number of four-time NFL MVP Aaron Rodgers, who passed for at least 290 yards (292) and multiple TDs (3) for the first time as a Pittsburgh Steeler in Sunday's 30-27 escape from the Cincinnati Bengals, who still haven't started 3-0 since 2015.

9. Number of consecutive games lost by the Indianapolis Colts, the longest skid in the league going back to last season … prior to Sunday's narrow victory over Houston.

10. Weird zero stat of the day: Cleveland Browns backup QB Shedeur Sanders completed his only pass of the day for 0 yards. That translates to a passer rating of 79.2, which is significantly better than Carolina Panthers counterpart Bryce Young's on Sunday (70.7, even though Young completed 26 of 48 passes for 291 yards, a TD and an INT). Sanders' 79.2 would have even led the league back in the old, pre-Super Bowl era (before 1966) days.

11. Weirdest zero stat of the day: Niners WR Deebo Samuel had 80 receiving yards and a TD in Sunday's win … despite finishing with zero receptions. Explanation? He scored the game's first touchdown on a hook-and-lateral with WR Mike Evans, who was credited with a 2-yard catch on the play.

HOOK-AND-LADDER TD 🤯

Deebo Samuel traveled a total distance of 110.35 yards and reached a max speed of 20.39 MPH on this 80-yard touchdown, per @NextGenStats @AZvsSF on FOX/FOX One
Stream on #NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/88dsZtSZum

11a. Samuel also iced San Francisco's 36-30 victory over the Arizona Cardinals with another uncredited catch.

Deebo ices it on the hands team 👏@AZvsSF on FOX/FOX One
Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/t32MJ70YM6

12. Number of consecutive games won by the Seahawks, the longest heater in the league going back to last season … prior to Sunday's loss to the Commanders. Seattle failed to become the third consecutive Super Bowl champion to begin its title defense with a 3-0 start.

13. Alternate uniforms < throwback uniforms.

It's merely a rule of thumb, not an immutable law. But if you saw the Bills ("Nickel City") and Colts ("Anvil Strike") unis on Sunday, then you'd probably agree that gray is a good color for baseball roadies … not so much for NFL uniforms.

The @BuffaloBills' "Nickel City" uniforms are ready for their debut. @LACvsBUF on FOX/FOX One
Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/SWjFLvF6Jw

14. However the Jacksonville Jaguars' throwbacks? Sweet. Can we get those back as the primaries?

The Jaguars "Prowler" throwbacks should be their primary uniforms. I will die on this hill without regrets. pic.twitter.com/7b7Sj2Kyhq

15. Speaking of bad looks, what's the tougher watch on TV: Indy's Lucas Oil Stadium with the roof open on a sunny day – like Sunday – or AT&T Stadium with the sun streaming through its western end-zone windows?

16. The Cowboys didn't have to deal with any glare – or even a bad field – Sunday while facing the Ravens at Maracanã Stadium in the league's first foray into Rio. But their problematic defense sabotaged them yet again – surrendering a 27-yard completion to Zay Flowers on the game's final game from scrimmage … before Ravens K Tyler Loop drilled the game-winning 56-yarder to secure a 34-31 victory. Still, this was a fantastic game and, who's to say, perhaps a Super Bowl 61 preview based on how this unpredictable season has unfolded so far.

17. Congratulations to Jaguars CB/WR Travis Hunter, who notched his first career interception Sunday … albeit on a – another – terrible throw by New England Patriots QB Drake Maye. Ten games into his career, Hunter, the insanely hyped dual-threat, Heisman Trophy-winning star from the University of Colorado, has one career pick and one career TD. I've been as skeptical as anyone about his pro prognosis, but good to see a player – and a great young man by many accounts – have a highlight moment.

TRAVIS HUNTER FIRST CAREER INT ‼️@NEvsJAX on CBS/Paramount+
Stream on #NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/tZFgPtUIf4

18. Did you know Jacksonville has a Brian Thomas Jr. and Bryan Thomas Jr. on its roster? Brian, the better-known wideout, had one catch for 8 yards in the Jags' 35-6 rout of the Patriots. Bryan, a defensive end, was credited with a tackle and half-sack of Maye.

19. Jaguars K Cam Little, who hit a 70-yard field goal in preseason last year and also broke the official record with a 68-yarder in the regular season last November, nearly hit a 70-yarder that counted right before halftime Sunday … but was wide right by inches. It's coming, though.

Cam Little attempts a record-breaking 70-yard field goal but it is no good.#NFL pic.twitter.com/obwBsaikJF

Cam Little thought his 70-yarder was good against the Patriots:

“Out of the 67, the 68, and the 70 that I’ve attempted, I by far hit that ball the cleanest by a mile.”#Jaguars #DUUUVAL @BrentASJax pic.twitter.com/3t6bA9wCZm

20. "Browns are gonna Browns?" Admittedly, I poked fun at first-year Cleveland coach Todd Monken for getting worked up about NBC analyst Mike Tomlin's dig prior to the Browns' win at Tampa last week. But maybe it's a positive phrase? Whatever you think of QB Deshaun Watson on a human level, he's got his team off to a 2-1 start after engineering Sunday's fourth-quarter win over the Panthers.

21. "Kinda poetic that I get this highlight," Tomlin said, the longtime Steelers coach, said on "Football Night in America," while breaking down the Browns' second consecutive win.

22. Watson, who's been a reviled figure in Cleveland essentially since his disastrous 2022 acquisition, was actually cheered Sunday, including when he returned after missing a play on a roughing penalty that preceded his game-winning TD pass to TE Harold Fannin Jr.

23. "I got a little teary-eyed feeling that energy because I put so much work to get back here, to be in this moment, to show that I can finish these games and get W's for the city and this organization," Watson said following the win.

24. The undefeated Raiders have already matched last season's win total (3), which is what allowed them to draft QB Fernando Mendoza atop the 2026 draft.

25. Not that Las Vegas has needed the 2025 Heisman Trophy winner as veteran Kirk Cousins has tossed three TDs in all three of the Silver and Black's victories, including Sunday's come-from-behind effort in New Orleans.

26. That's because the Saints had been dominant in the fourth quarter, outscoring opponents 25-3 in the final period over the first two weeks. But the Raiders outpointed them 13-0 in the fourth in Sunday's 35-27 win at the Superdome.

27. And while second-year Saints QB Tyler Shough threw four TD passes Sunday, he also turned the ball over three times, giving Cousins and the Raiders the margin for error they needed to snatch the victory.

28. Call the Raiders' start fluky if you want, but remember that Sunday was the first game this season in which they had, arguably, their best player – TE Brock Bowers making his 2026 debut to the tune of 10 catches, 116 yards and a TD. He missed the first two weeks after undergoing a meniscus trim.

29. Call the Vikings' 3-0 start fluky if you want – especially in light of injuries to QB Kyler Murray, WR Justin Jefferson (Sunday) and others. They also needed a punt return for a TD in their 23-16 win at Tampa on Sunday. But that Minnesota D is vicious – racking up six sacks and 12 QB hits Sunday while knocking Bucs QB Baker Mayfield from the game.

30. If you didn't know, Mayfield's backup is undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels, who threw a pick among three incompletions in his pro debut. The Bucs' ship sure appears to be sinking fast while going to the bottom of the NFC South standings, especially after Mayfield suffered a dislocated thumb on his throwing hand.

31. A reminder to all NFL players, officials and writers: "You guys better get your (expletive) together" … which is what referee Ronald Torbert told his crew (on a hot mic) during Sunday's game in Indianapolis, per the Associated Press.

32. Last and, sadly, least – the Dolphins. Not only are the Fins winless, they haven't come closer than 14 points to a victory. Perhaps worse, RB De'Von Achane, their best player, suffered a knee injury that seems to be serious, coach Jeff Hafley admitting a lack of optimism about Achane's prognosis. Could we be witnessing the first 0-17 outfit in NFL history?
