title: Jadarian Price’s fumble issues are not new
description: Jadarian Price’s fumbles to start his NFL career are a continuation of a college concern.
fullText:
The Seattle Seahawks have been blessed with tremendous ball security from their main running backs over the past few seasons. Kenneth Walker III never lost a fumble with the Seahawks and only had one career fumble on an actual run play, while Zach Charbonnet's next fumble will be his first.

Walker is on another team (and looking like a viable Offensive Player of the Year candidate) while Charbonnet isn't back for at least another two weeks. The Seahawks are relying on Jadarian Price to be an immediate contributor as a first-round pick. He's shown some flashes of explosive runs and an ability to be a receiving threat out of the backfield, so there's been a good helping of promising plays.

He's also put the ball on the ground twice in as many weeks.

.@ZavenCollins liked what he saw 😳#SEAvsAZ | 📺 FOX pic.twitter.com/QHufimdBab

FUMBLE 🚨@SEAvsWAS on FOX/FOX One
Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/RNgk2tQRjX

The second fumble was enough for the Seahawks to bench him until the two-minute drill of the first half of their 33-31 loss to the Washington Commanders. It might seem like tough love, but Price is a rookie and he doesn't have the same leeway as more established running backs.

"I think just as a team, if we turn the ball over, it's not good business," Mike Macdonald said after the game. "So, when you come back after the initial fumble, we decide to calm it down and bring it back after the half. He's gonna be fine. He's gonna figure it out, he'll be fine."

"I made a mistake," Price said. "Just got to deal with the consequences."

Price only carried the ball two more times and had just six total touches for 21 yards. It was a day in which the Seahawks generated almost nothing on the ground, so it wasn't like Emanuel Wilson or George Holani were significantly better.

But the fumbling for Price is not a new issue. It was brought up in his final season at Notre Dame, in which he fumbled three times (losing two) on just 113 carries. All of his fumbles last year were inside the opposition 10, with C.J. Carr preventing a hat trick of red zone turnovers. That may or may not be why Seattle has been hesitant to give him the ball in goal-to-go situations.

Adding his 12 games in his final Notre Dame season, Price has five fumbles in 15 games. That's five fumbles over 141 carries, or one on every 28 attempts. In effect, that's two games worth of carries for Price. James Cook of the Buffalo Bills led all running backs in the NFL with six fumbles last season, except that's on 309 carries and he did a little thing called leading the league in rushing yards. Price hasn't quite built up that sort of equity to where the fumbles are a minor story due to terrific productivity.

This is not an indictment of the pick or an indication that this is who Price will always be. But for someone who was not the primary back at Notre Dame and hasn't even had the bulk of the carries as a pro, this is a legitimate concern until he fixes it. I trust that Price will be able to work on this as he develops, but it's a weakness in his game that opposition defenses are going to relentlessly attack. And this, never mind any pass protection concerns, might affect his workload until he earns the trust of the coaching staff.

title: NFL betting, odds: Tampa Bay Buccaneers set a new record for betting futility, losing 12th straight game against the spread
description: The Bucs have failed to cover the spread in 12 straight games, a new NFL record.
fullText:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers closed as small home underdog against the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday in Week 3. Baker Mayfield injured his thumb in the fourth quarter and Tampa Bay lost 23-16, despite the Vikings generating only nine first downs and going 2-of-15 on third down. Minnesota also only scored one offensive touchdown.

Tampa Bay fell to 2-10 in its last 12 games dating back to last season. More significant for bettors, though, the Bucs again didn't cover the spread — the 12th straight game in which that's occurred.

The ATS loss set the NFL record for the most consecutive games a team has failed to cover the spread in the Super Bowl era. Tampa Bay surpassed the 11-game mark of spread-covering futility established by the 1983-84 Houston Oilers, per the Action Network.

The losses against the number have come in all shapes and sizes, as Tampa Bay has failed to cover in four games during the streak as an underdog, seven games at home and two as a road favorite.

The last time the Bucs won a game against the spread in Week 8 last season (Oct. 26, 2025) when Tampa Bay beat New Orleans 23-3 as a 3.5-point road favorite.

With Mayfield likely out, the Bucs opened as a 3-point home underdog against the Green Bay Packers. Rookie QB Jalon Daniels will get the start if Mayfield can't go.

title: 3 games, 3 wins: Joe Brady makes NFL history
description: At 37, Brady became the fifth-youngest NFL head coach to win his first three games
fullText:
Joe Brady is three games into his NFL head-coaching career, and he still hasn't lost one.

The Buffalo Bills beat the Los Angeles Chargers 24-16 on Sunday, improving to 3-0 under Brady and putting their new head coach in some pretty exclusive company in the process.

At 37 years old, Brady became the fifth-youngest head coach in NFL history to begin his career with three straight wins. Only Josh McDaniels, John Madden, Bill Cowher, and Mike Tomlin were younger when they started 3-0.

McDaniels and Madden were both 33 when they reached the mark, while Cowher and Tomlin were 35.

Brady had already made a little franchise history one week earlier. Buffalo's win over Detroit made him the first head coach in Bills history to win each of his first two regular-season games at the helm. Sunday's win pushed the streak to three and moved the accomplishment beyond the Buffalo record book.

Brady turned 37 on Wednesday, making him the youngest active head coach in the NFL. According to Bills PR, he is also the second-youngest head coach or manager across the NFL, MLB, NBA, and NHL, behind only 34-year-old Washington Nationals manager Blake Butera.

Bills HC Joe Brady turns 37 today. 

Brady is the youngest active HC in the NFL and is the second-youngest coach across the MLB/NBA/NFL/NHL, behind only Washington Nationals' manager Blake Butera (34 years old). pic.twitter.com/aJdPRmBxiZ

Brady took over as Buffalo's head coach after spending the previous two-plus seasons running the Bills' offense, first as interim offensive coordinator during the 2023 season and then in the permanent role.

Now, three games into his first head-coaching job, Brady has three wins. That means his usual postgame message needs another update.

title: Steve Sarkisian blames "society" for Colin Simmons's bizarre unsportsmanlike conduct foul
description: To cap a week in which the NFL went overboard with fines, Texas defensive end Colin Simmons did something that possibly would have gotten him banned for life by 345 Park Avenue.
fullText:
To cap a week in which the NFL went overboard with fines, Texas defensive end Colin Simmons did something that possibly would have gotten him banned for life by 345 Park Avenue.

After one of his Longhorn record-tying five sacks against Tennessee, Simmons celebrated by pretending to urinate on the field.

He seemed surprised when the officials penalized the move, with the eventual explanation being that Simmons was "simulating using the restroom."

Coach Steve Sarkisian addressed the situation following the 20-17 win.

"We took him out," Sarkisian said, via Tyler Lauletta of Awful Announcing, regarding the fact that Simmons, well, took it out. "We addressed it, and put him back in. I'm not gonna give the guy the death penalty over an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty. We've got to fix it though. That can't continue as we move forward."

That part is reasonable and appropriate. Then, things got a little screwy from Sarkisian.

"Unfortunately, in our society right now, we live in the 'look at me' society," Sarkisian said. "All of you guys have your Twitter accounts, and as fast as you can type something because you want everyone to look at your account, and you get clicks. Well, that's the world that we live in. So we've got to get to —it's about the team and focus on the team, and not so much 'look at me.' So we'll try to improve upon that, but five sacks was pretty cool today too."

Steve, don't simulate using the restroom on our leg and tell us it's raining. Society didn't lead Simmons to do something we've never seen a player do, because 99.999999 percent of all players know not to do it.

Still, we'd love to hear how Sarkisian would explain a similarly perverse celebration that was not penalized. Almost as much as we'd love to hear the explanation of the foul.

title: Oregon Quarterback Dante Moore Leaves Game in Ambulance After Being Knocked Out with Brutal Hit to the Head

fullText:
Dante Moore was injured during a game against the USC Trojans after taking a severe hit to the head

The Oregon quarterback, 21, was stretchered off the field and taken to a waiting ambulance following the hit

Moore, a top 2027 NFL Draft prospect, transferred to Oregon in 2023 and has led the team to a 2-1 record

University of Oregon quarterback Dante Moore was taken off the field after taking a severe hit to the head.

During the Ducks' Saturday, Sept. 26, game against the University of Southern California Trojans in Los Angeles, the star quarterback, 21, scrambled on a play in the second quarter.

He took a slide, per USA Today, and USC linebacker Desman Stephen II hit him, sending his head slamming into the ground. Referees threw a flag, and Moore could be seen lying on the ground as Oregon staff rushed onto the field.

OMG terrifying hit on Dante Moore as he's sliding, hope he's ok pic.twitter.com/btSngnriAZ

Moore was placed on a stretcher after a few minutes with the entire Oregon team by his side, and USC quarterback Jayden Maiava also came to check on him. Moore was then put inside a waiting ambulance, and he did not appear to be moving, per CBS Sports.

NBC broadcast announcers shared just after halftime that Moore had been taken to a local hospital and was being evaluated by doctors.

Meanwhile, a fight nearly broke out as Oregon players confronted USC defenders, and officials and coaches tried to break it up. Linebacker Stephen received a targeting penalty and was disqualified, and offsetting unsportsmanlike conduct flags were assessed to both teams for the scuffle.

Moore, originally from East Cleveland, Ohio, began his college career at UCLA in January 2023, and by December of that year, he announced he would transfer to Oregon. Although he was considered a top prospect for the 2026 NFL Draft, Moore did not enter the draft and opted to go back to school.

The star quarterback started his season this year as a potential starting quarterback in the 2027 NFL Draft and has led Oregon to a 2-1 record thus far. He had thrown for 849 yards and nine touchdowns leading into Saturday's game, per ESPN.

Dylan Raiola took over Oregon's offense after Moore exited the field. Raiola, 21, started his two previous seasons at Nebraska before transferring to Oregon this offseason.

title: Sloppy start to NFL season 'super frustrating' for Tony Dungy | Exclusive
description: Tony Dungy was connected to the NFL for 46 years as a player, coach and broadcaster. He has a different view this season.
fullText:
Tony Dungy is watching the NFL with a different purpose these days – there's no game plan to execute or strategy to analyze for millions of viewers on live TV – and the Hall of Fame coach is not so thrilled.

The first two weeks of the NFL season have left Dungy bemoaning sloppy football that reminds him of the preseason.

"Super frustrating to me," Dungy told USA TODAY Sports this week. "I think people are doing a disservice to their team by not playing players in the preseason, not getting them ready. I've seen guys who looked like they were not ready for the speed of the game because they didn't play in the preseason.

"I don't think it will be until October when we can say who's good and who isn't because I think a lot of these teams are still getting ready to play."

Dungy said that as a coach, he can understand the rationale behind not playing starters – and particularly quarterbacks – during preseason. It's the injury risk. Except for the teams that play in the Hall of Fame Game, teams play just three preseason games. And about half the teams didn't put their starting quarterback on the field in preseason.

When Dungy coached (through the 2008 season), teams played four preseason games and his starters typically played about six quarters across the contests. Starters – including his franchise quarterback – would go for about three quarters in the third preseason game, then sit out the preseason finale.

"I cannot imagine, if I told Peyton Manning, 'Hey, you're not going to play at all, the first snap of the regular season is going to be your first live snap,' I don't think he would have been very happy about that," Dungy said. "Now, a lot of people are doing it."

That's not all that Dungy, 70, is getting used to. This is the first time in 46 years that he hasn't been connected to the NFL as a player, coach or broadcaster. The past 17 years he served as an analyst for "Football Night in America," part of the "Sunday Night Football" package on NBC, but Dungy and former all-pro safety Rodney Harrison were not renewed as part of a revamped show that now includes former Steelers coach Mike Tomlin.

"They felt it was time," Dungy said. "Whether they wanted to be younger, whether they wanted to have different voices, I don't know. Rodney and I were there 17 years. We had a lot of fun together and I made some great friendships. It was special to me because I got to maintain a lot of relationships and see people and talk to guys and kind of stay in the game without being in it 24/7.

"I just look at now like God's got another plan and something else, and it'll be a different phase. But it was a neat 17 years."

Coincidentally, Dungy also wasn't retained after six years as a member of the Pro Football Hall of Fame Selection committee. The size of the committee was reduced from 50 voters to 25 (plus three alternates) as part of sweeping changes.

"I'm not bitter or upset or anything about not being on," Dungy said. "They asked for my time on the committee, I did it, I enjoyed it. It wasn't easy, but it was something I felt good about doing."

Dungy, a devout Christian who lives in Tampa, is eager to continue walking the walk of a faith that he has publicly professed throughout his career – and sometimes drawn criticism for. Given his numerous charity efforts, spiritual outreach and potential media projects, there won't be much of a void, if any, on his calendar without his national TV job.

On Saturday, Dungy will conduct the chapel service for the Minnesota Vikings after their arrival in town. He also spoke to the football team at Central Florida and this week conducted a Zoom chat with Wake Forest's baseball team.

"In the past, I'd have to say I couldn't do it in the fall because I'm occupied," he said.

Dungy is also brainstorming with James Brown, the host of CBS' "NFL Today" and his longtime friend, about developing a faith-based podcast. And he's taped about 10 interviews with players and coaches for a project being shopped, dubbed "Road to Sunday," that will delve into backstories essential to their journeys.

"All of them talked about the Lord without being asked. It was crazy!" Dungy said of the interviews. "To be able to talk about what guys are doing off the field, what's on their heart, what's inspired them and how they got there, who was key in their lives, I think we can tell some positive sports stories that the world needs."

In the meantime, Dungy will still see the NFL through the eyes of a coach, analyst and player.

"I saw the Bucs play on TV and they had four fumbles," he said, referring to the Week 1 loss at Cincinnati. "It just looked like guys are not ready for contact. And I saw a lot of blown coverages, people going in motion and getting wide open. I saw a lot of tackling that looked like what you'd do at practice – where you hit the guys but you don't wrap them up. You let them keep running and you don't take people to the ground. It looked like the same thing.

"I know they are going to be better, they are going to be sharper, and it's a long season. But these first two weeks, I've seen a lot of up and down play that you don't expect."

At this point, Dungy says that offenses – with timing sharpened by 7-on-7 non-contract drills – have a distinct advantage over defenses.

"In the old days, it used to be the opposite," he said.

Interestingly, Dungy said that he and Tomlin – who was hired by Dungy an a NFL coach and now replaces him on the NBC set – talked about how defenses are hard-pressed to keep up because CBA rules limit contact in practices.

Of course, it's no surprise that Dungy – a college quarterback who converted to safety in the NFL and former defensive coordinator – has a nerve struck for defense.

"The way the practice schedules are set up, with what you can and can't do, it's harder on defense," Dungy said. "It's hard to get that physicalness, the reaction time and everything.

"I look at Denver and Houston as two of the best defenses last year and they both had most of their guys back. And they're giving up 30 points in a game (in Week 1). You're saying, 'Wait a minute. Are these the same guys?' They are, but they're not playing the same way. So I think some of these teams are going to be what they were and some may not."

Either way, it will be a different type of must-see TV for Dungy.

title: Seahawks safety Julian Love an NFL leader in key stat

title: Chiefs OC Eric Bieniemy cracks joke about Travis Kelce getting married to Taylor Swift

fullText:
Kansas City Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy definitely feels Taylor Swift has had a positive impact on Travis Kelce.

Travis Kelce has had a strong start to the NFL season, proving that he was right to continue playing despite some calling for him to retire.

The three-time Super Bowl champion has helped the Kansas City Chiefs go 2-0, reigniting his connection with fit-again quarterback Patrick Mahomes.

Chiefs OC Eric Bieniemy says he loves Travis Kelce's approach and how committed he is to the team despite his huge public profile.

But he did make a quick joke about Kelce 'marrying up' with his summer wedding to Taylor Swift.

Bieniemy told a press conference: "I know he's become this big time mega star, well I think he married up but he's always remained the same.

"He provides leadership to our guys, he provides the necessary energy."

Travis Kelce has hit the headlines over the past year for what he wears every time he steps out, for every single minute detail of his wedding, and even his podcast.

So it must be nice for him to get back on the football field.

Stephen A. Smith joked that marriage often slows men down, but it seems to have had a galvanising effect on Travis Kelce.

It is only two games, but Kelce looked in playoff form during the overtime win over the Colts, racking up 101 yards.

title: Chargers rumors: NFL insider reveals teams could call about Justin Herbert trade
description: The Chargers could be getting calls on Justin Herbert if their season continues to trend the wrong way.
fullText:
The Chargers are unlikely to trade Justin Herbert, but they could start getting calls on him if the season keeps going sideways.

NFL insider Tom Pelissero appeared on The Rich Eisen Show and said he wouldn't be surprised if the Chargers start getting calls on Herbert if the team doesn't turn things around.

"Right now, the LA Chargers are 0-2. You look at their upcoming schedule: if they're 1-5 or 0-6, I don't think they'll trade Justin Herbert, but you can bet they're going to get calls about Justin Herbert because why not," Pelissero said.

"Bad teams: if you're having a bad season, people are going to sit there and try to take advantage of you and go after your good players. That's where the way the season plays out is going to determine a whole lot of different things, and the more quarterbacks get hurt, the more the price might go up."

Herbert and the Chargers are off to a horrendous start to the season. They sit at 0-2, having lost their first two games to two of the league's worst teams (at least from last season), the Cardinals and Raiders.

The 28-year-old quarterback hasn't done himself any favors in those losses either.

Herbert's overall numbers and overall output have received major scrutiny, and rightfully so. He's on pace for a career low in completion percentage at 59.3%, throwing only two touchdowns, three interceptions, and 401 yards through two games.

Mike McDaniel's offense was supposed to take the Chargers to another level; instead, they look lost, and Herbert seems to look uncomfortable.

The Chargers have a gauntlet of a schedule ahead, starting in Week 3 against the Bills. Things don't look promising after what was expected to be a promising season.

Nonetheless, the Chargers still have plenty of football left to turn this around.
